# Fractalstyler Closed-World Design Rules

1. **Closed-World Styling Law**:
   Styles are added ONLY via fractal composition and existing tokens.
   - NO scoped <style> blocks anywhere in components.
   - NO inline style="..." attributes.
   - NO raw hex colors (#fff).
   - NO arbitrary pixel dimensions (>2px).
   - NO child combinators (> * is forbidden; selectors are plain descendants).

2. **Layer Architecture** — the stylesheets, in cascade order:
   - configurations.css: global tokens (layout dimensions, z-index bands, font stacks) and the base resets.
   - gaps-pads-margins.css: the space ladder (.gap-*, .rgap-*, .cgap-*, .pad-*, .px-*, .py-*, .mar-*, .mx-*, .my-* across 8 steps).
   - shapes-sizes.css: radius channels (.radius-xs..full), control heights (.h-xs..h-3xl), sizing helpers (.wfull, .hfull, .min0).
   - containers.css: .box (col), .row (horizontal), .grid with physical modifiers (.xcenter, .ycenter, .xbetween), positioning, stacking, scroll containers, .grid-1..6, .cspan-1..8, .card-grid, .prose, frames, .reel.
   - typography.css: .text-xs..5xl, roles (.page-title, .nav-link), .weight-*, .lh*, .ls-*, alignment.
   - border-elevation-focus.css: .border, the per-side partitions (.bt, .br, .bb, .bl), elevation (.shad-xs..3xl), focus rings.
   - layout-shell.css: .app-shell, .app-header, .app-main, .app-footer, .sidebar-left, .sidebar-right, .content-section.
   - colors-themes.css: surface fills (.bg, .bg-surface, .bg-panel), ink (.text-primary, .text-muted), status colours, borders.
   - motion-animation.css: .anim-spin, .anim-pulse, .anim-fade-in, .anim-fade-out.
   - components.css: buttons, inputs, selects, links, tags, badges, avatars, switches, checkboxes.
   - component-props.css: the variant classes (.primary, .secondary, .themed, .outline, .ghost, .link, .info, .success, .warning, .danger), shape props (.rect, .min, .modern, .curved, .round) and height props (.h-xs..h-xl).
   - responsive.css: .md-only, .lg-only, .xl-only and their -hide counterparts.
   - custom.css: the sanctioned extension point — project skins, the .mascot* family.

2b. **Variants are direct classes**:
   There is no attribute axis: a button is styled by the classes it carries.
   `<button class="button primary h-md">` — the same variant classes work on
   a button, an input, a select, a card or a div.

3. **Verification**:
   Always verify with:
   - pnpm registry # regenerates registry.json and registry.md — REQUIRED, this server validates against it
   - pnpm lint   # contract & token purity linter
   - pnpm check  # svelte diagnostics & deck validator
   - pnpm build  # package + publint

4. **Icons**: come from the `fractalicons` package only. Never inline SVG or unicode glyphs.
```

1	# AGENTS
2	
3	name - fractalstyler
4	description - A composition styling system, shipped as plain CSS. The class registry is the public API: compose in markup, write no stylesheet.
5	type - sveltekit
6	gitlink - https://github.com/fractalmandala/fractalstyler
7	npmlink - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler
8	url - https://fractalsvelte.dev/fractalstyler
9	
10	---
11	
12	## What this package is
13	
14	A **closed-world** styling system. It ships plain CSS layers, a generated
15	registry of every class, a linter, and an MCP server. There are no mixins, no
16	styling functions, and no "add your own CSS" — a project composes the system
17	from the classes that exist, and nothing else.
18	
19	**The registry is the API.** If a class is not in the registry, it does not
20	exist, and using it is a bug — not a style choice.
21	
22	## The rules
23	
24	These are what the linter enforces, and what an agent must not break:
25	
26	1. **Compose in markup.** Only classes from the registry. No new class names,
27	   ever — even for one element.
28	2. **No scoped `<style>` blocks** in components. Components are markup and
29	   logic only.
30	3. **No inline `style="…"` attributes.** Inline styles are invisible to the
31	   registry, unreachable by a theme switch, and unaccounted for.
32	4. **No raw hex colours.** Every colour resolves through a semantic token —
33	   `var(--bg)`, `var(--text-primary)`, `var(--border)`.
34	5. **No arbitrary pixels.** Only 1–2px (hairlines, borders) may be literal;
35	   everything else rides the `--space-*` ladder.
36	6. **Corners go through the radius ladder** — `var(--radius-*)`, never a
37	   literal `border-radius`.
38	7. **Every `var(--token)` must resolve** to a token that exists.
39	8. **Icons come from `fractalicons`** — never inline SVG, never unicode glyphs.
40	
41	A class that does not exist yet is a **request for a new class**, not a
42	licence to invent one. See *When the system cannot express it* below.
43	
44	## Where the truth lives
45	
46	| | |
47	|:---|:---|
48	| **[`registry.md`](./registry.md)** | every class — what it does, what declares it, and a piece of markup to copy. **Read this before writing markup.** |
49	| [`registry.json`](./registry.json) | the same thing for machines; the linter and the MCP validate against it |
50	| [`docs/`](./docs/README.md) | one page per stylesheet — the reasoning, not just the list |
51	| [`docs/introduction.md`](./docs/introduction.md) | the mental model: containers, modifiers, the ladders, the vocabulary |
52	| [`skills/fractalstyler/SKILL.md`](./skills/fractalstyler/SKILL.md) | the agent skill — the rules in the form an agent should follow |
53	| [`docs/14-development.md`](./docs/14-development.md) | how the package itself is built, and how to publish an update |
54	| [`docs/16-layout.md`](./docs/16-layout.md) | the shell components (`AppShell`, `NavSection`, …) and the layout state |
55	
56	The vocabulary, in one screen:
57	
58	| | |
59	|:---|:---|
60	| Containers | `.box` (column), `.row` (horizontal), `.grid` — and their modifiers `.xcenter`, `.ycenter`, `.xbetween` |
61	| Spacing | `.gap-*`, `.pad-*`, `.px-*`, `.py-*`, `.mar-*` — eight steps: `xs sm md bs lg xl 2xl 3xl` |
62	| Type | `.text-xs` … `.text-5xl`, `.weight-*`, `.lh*`, `.ls-*`, `.truncate` |
63	| Colour | `.bg`, `.bg-surface`, `.text-primary`, `.text-muted`, `.border` — roles, never values |
64	| Variants | `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.themed`, `.outline`, `.ghost`, `.link` |
65	| Shape & height | `.rect`, `.mincurved`, `.modern`, `.curved`, `.round` · `.h-xs` … `.h-xl` |
66	
67	**Modifiers are never standalone.** `.xcenter` resolves only on a container —
68	`.row.xcenter`, not a bare `.xcenter`.
69	
70	## Using it in a project
71	
72	```sh
73	pnpm add -D @fractaldesign/fractalstyler
74	```
75	
76	```js
77	// one import — the bundler inlines the layers in cascade order
78	import '@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/styles';
79	```
80	
81	Or a single layer, when only part of the system is wanted:
82	
83	```js
84	import '@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/styles/typography.css';
85	```
86	
87	The shell components are published too:
88	
89	```js
90	import { AppShell, layoutState } from '@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/layout';
91	```
92	
93	**Node 22.18 or newer** is required — the package ships TypeScript and runs it
94	through a launcher (`runtime/run.mjs`).
95	
96	## The MCP server — an agent's co-pilot
97	
98	An agent that knows the system does not have to guess a class name. The MCP
99	server exposes the registry, the tokens and the contract as tools.
100	
101	```sh
102	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler mcp
103	```
104	
105	```json
106	{
107	  "mcpServers": {
108	    "fractalstyler": {
109	      "command": "npx",
110	      "args": ["-y", "@fractaldesign/fractalstyler", "mcp"]
111	    }
112	  }
113	}
114	```
115	
116	| Tool | Use it for |
117	|:---|:---|
118	| `guide_styling` | the guidance for a stated intent — spacing, layout, type, colour |
119	| `search_classes` | finding the class that does the job — by name, description or property |
120	| `get_tokens` | the token scales — space, type, radius, shadow, surfaces |
121	| `snap_to_tokens` | snapping a raw pixel value (from a mockup) to the nearest token |
122	| `css_to_classes` | finding the classes that produce a given piece of CSS |
123	| `lint_markup` | checking markup before it ships |
124	| `get_system_rules` | the closed-world rules themselves |
125	
126	Two prompts: `design_component` (plan and author a component) and
127	`audit_markup` (audit existing markup).
128	
129	**The order that works:** `search_classes` → write the markup → `lint_markup`
130	→ ship. Never write markup from memory.
131	
132	## The linter
133	
134	```sh
135	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler lint          # audit this project
136	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler lint src/     # audit a directory
137	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler lint --json   # machine-readable, for CI
138	```
139	
140	| Rule | Severity | What it catches |
141	|:---|:---|:---|
142	| `fs/no-in-component-styles` | error | a scoped `<style>` block |
143	| `fs/no-inline-styles` | error | a `style="…"` attribute |
144	| `fs/unknown-class` | error | a class that is not in the registry |
145	| `fs/token-purity` | error | a raw hex, a pixel outside the 1–2px budget, an unresolved `var()` |
146	| `fs/sass-nesting` | error | `&` in a plain `.css` file — the browser drops the whole rule |
147	| `fs/hardcoded-radius` | warning | a literal `border-radius` the shape axis cannot reach |
148	
149	**Never silence the linter to make it pass.** An `unknown-class` error means
150	one of three things, and only one of them is a change to the system:
151	
152	1. the class name is wrong → use the right one (`search_classes`);
153	2. the class is needed but missing → **add it to the system** (below);
154	3. the class belongs to the project → put it in `custom.css`, the sanctioned
155	   extension layer, and it joins the registry.
156	
157	The linter reads `registry.json` and the stylesheets. If the registry is stale,
158	it is stale for the linter too — run `npm run registry` in the package.
159	
160	## When the system cannot express it
161	
162	Do not work around it. Work in the system:
163	
164	1. Check whether an existing token and existing classes already compose what
165	   is needed — `search_classes`, `get_tokens`.
166	2. If a **new utility class** is genuinely needed, add it to the layer that
167	   owns it in `src/lib/styles/`, give it a name in the system's voice, and
168	   regenerate the registry.
169	3. If it is **project-specific** (branding, a mascot, a third-party skin), it
170	   belongs in `src/lib/styles/custom.css` — the sanctioned extension point.
171	   Every class there joins the registry.
172	4. If it is **missing from the design system itself**, that is a change to
173	   Fractalstyler, not to the project.
174	
175	## The CLI
176	
177	```sh
178	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler init     # scaffold: track the package or eject the styles
179	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler eject    # copy the styles + the registry builder into the project
180	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler lint     # the contract linter
181	npx @fractaldesign/fractalstyler mcp      # the MCP server
182	```
183	
184	`init` with no flags asks; `--yes` takes the defaults. Nothing is ever
185	overwritten — a file you already have is kept and reported.
186	
187	## Developing this package
188	
189	```sh
190	npm run dev            # the demo site
191	npm run check          # type-check + validate the docs + lint the components
192	npm run build          # the publishable package
193	```
194	
195	### The scripts, and when to run them
196	
197	| You changed… | Run |
198	|:---|:---|
199	| a class in `src/lib/styles/*.css` | `npm run registry` |
200	| a token in `src/lib/styles/*.css` | `npm run tokens` |
201	| the docs, the skill, the README | `npm run validate:deck` |
202	| anything, before you commit | `npm run check` |
203	| a new stylesheet | `npm run registry` — and add it to `src/lib/styles/index.css` **and** to `FILE_ORDER` in `scripts/update-registry.ts`; the two must agree |
204	| nothing, publishing | `npm run build` |
205	
206	`npm run registry` regenerates `registry.json`, `registry.md` and the two skill
207	references. `npm run tokens` regenerates `src/lib/tokensRegistry.ts`. Neither
208	file is ever edited by hand — they carry a "Generated" banner.
209	
210	### The layout of the package
211	
212	| | |
213	|:---|:---|
214	| `src/lib/styles/` | the layers — the system itself. Plain CSS, one file per concern |
215	| `src/lib/styles/index.css` | the cascade: the order the layers are concatenated in |
216	| `src/lib/styles/custom.css` | the sanctioned extension layer |
217	| `src/lib/layout/` | the shell components |
218	| `src/lib/components/` | the sveltemodular workspace app — **in progress, not part of the contract yet** |
219	| `scripts/` | the generator, the token generator, the parser, the doc validator |
220	| `lint/` | the contract linter |
221	| `mcp/` | the MCP server |
222	| `cli/` | the consumer-facing CLI |
223	| `runtime/run.mjs` | the launcher that lets Node run the shipped TypeScript |
224	
225	## Before you update, and how to publish
226	
227	**Before changing anything:**
228	
229	1. Run `npm run check` — the tree must be clean.
230	2. If the change touches a stylesheet, a token or the docs, run the script
231	   from the table above and **commit the regenerated files with the change**.
232	3. Never edit `registry.json`, `registry.md`, `skills/fractalstyler/references/*`
233	   or `src/lib/tokensRegistry.ts` by hand — they are generated.
234	
235	**To publish:**
236	
237	```sh
238	npm version minor      # or patch — regenerates the registry and tokens, commits, tags
239	git push --follow-tags
240	npm publish            # prepack builds and validates; publint must pass
241	```
242	
243	The version constant in `src/lib/index.ts` is hand-written — keep it in step
244	with `package.json`.
245	
246	**Do not push or publish unless the user asks.** Committing and tagging is
247	step one of publishing, so the same rule applies.
248	
249	## House rules
250	
251	1. Every project must have `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and — where it applies —
252	   `DESIGN.md`, and a `LICENSE` when it is published.
253	2. The README of every project must open with: name, description, type, and
254	   where relevant gitlink, npmlink, url.
255	3. The README must carry the commands to run dev, build, and run the app.
256	4. When a project starts using Fractalstyler: add it to
257	   `/Users/amrit/ars-docs/alldocs/04canonicals/project-tracker.json`.
258	5. Do not initiate git or push to GitHub unless the user instructs it.
259	6. When developing, load and use poteto-mode —

1	---
2	name: fractalstyler
3	description: Build, compose, modify, or audit UI interfaces using the closed Fractalstyler composition styling system. Use whenever authoring HTML, Svelte, CSS, or TS/JS components where new ad-hoc classes, scoped style blocks, inline styles, custom properties, or arbitrary CSS are strictly forbidden.
4	---
5	
6	# Fractalstyler Styling System & Style Guard
7	
8	Operate within the `fractalstyler` registry as a **closed world**. Never invent a class or styling definition, even when the requested design is not immediately obvious.
9	
10	## Mandatory Agent Workflow
11	
12	1. **Consult the Registry First**:
13	   Read `registry.md` or `references/fractals.md`. Search for existing utility classes, container bases, layouts, and shells before writing any markup.
14	2. **Compose Only from Verified Classes**:
15	   - Containers: `.box` (column), `.row` (horizontal), `.grid` (CSS grid).
16	   - Physical Alignment: **modifiers, never standalone** — they only resolve on a container: `.row.xcenter`, `.box.ycenter`, `.grid.xbetween`. There is no bare `.xcenter`.
17	   - Dimensions & Spacing: `.gap-*`/`.rgap-*`/`.cgap-*`, `.pad-*`, `.px-*` (inline) / `.py-*` (block) / `.pt-*` `.pr-*` `.pb-*` `.pl-*`, `.mar-*`/`.mx-*`/`.my-*`, `.wfull`/`.hfull`, `.h-xs`…`.h-xl`. **There is no `.pad-x-*`, `.pad-y-*` or `.w-*`.**
18	   - Visuals: `.bg`, `.bg-surface`, `.bg-panel`, `.bg-input`, `.bg-button`, `.bg-success`/`.bg-warning`/`.bg-danger`/`.bg-info`, `.border` (+`-subtle`/`-strong`), per-side `.bt`/`.br`/`.bb`/`.bl` (+`-str`/`-sub`), `.radius-*`, `.shad-*`. **There is no `.border-top`/`.border-bottom`.**
19	   - Typography: `.text-xs` .. `.text-5xl`, `.weight-300`…`.weight-800`, `.truncate`.
20	   - Layouts: `.grid-1`…`.grid-6`, `.cspan-1`…`.cspan-8`, `.card-grid`, `.prose`, `.prose-left`, `.frame-16-9`…, `.reel`.
21	   - Interactions: `button` (or the equivalent `.button` class), `a.btn`, `.input`, `.select`, `.button-group`, `.split-button`, `.tag`, `.badge`, `.avatar-group`.
22	3. **Variants are direct classes** — there is no attribute axis and no `data-variant`:
23	   - The variant, the shape and the height are classes on the element itself:
24	   | What | Classes |
25	   |:---|:---|
26	   | Variant | `.primary` `.secondary` `.themed` `.outline` `.ghost` `.link` `.info` `.success` `.warning` `.danger` |
27	   | Shape | `.rect` `.mincurved` `.modern` `.curved` `.round` |
28	   | Height | `.h-xs` `.h-sm` `.h-md` `.h-bs` `.h-lg` `.h-xl` |
29	   - The same classes work on a button, an input, a select, a card or a div: `<button class="button primary h-md">`.
30	4. **Hard Boundaries**:
31	   - **NO in-component `<style>` blocks**: Components must remain pure markup and logic.
32	   - **NO inline `style="..."` attributes**: Inline styles are unconstrained ad-hoc CSS.
33	   - **NO raw hex colors (`#hex`)**: Every color must resolve through semantic tokens (`var(--bg)`, `var(--text-primary)`, `var(--border)`, etc.).
34	   - **NO arbitrary pixel dimensions (>2px)**: Literal pixels bypass the dimension ladder. Only 1-2px (borders, hairlines) may be literal.
35	   - **Icons come from `fractalicons`**: never inline SVG or unicode glyphs.
36	5. **Mandatory Verification**:
37	   Before claiming task completion, always execute:
38	   ```bash
39	   pnpm lint
40	   pnpm check
41	   ```
42	   Both checks must pass with 0 errors.
43	
44	
45	## Progressive Discovery Index
46	
47	| Styling Task | File to Inspect | Responsibility |
48	|:---|:---|:---|
49	| Active files and cascade order | `src/lib/styles/index.css` | Master composition contract. |
50	| Global tokens, z-index, fonts, base resets | `src/lib/styles/configurations.css` | Layout dimensions and element defaults. |
51	| Spacing, gaps, padding, margins | `src/lib/styles/gaps-pads-margins.css` | The space ladder. |
52	| Radius, control heights, sizing | `src/lib/styles/shapes-sizes.css` | Shape channels and sizing helpers. |
53	| Flex/grid containers, axis alignment, responsive grids | `src/lib/styles/containers.css` | Structural containers plus grid, frame and reel helpers. |
54	| Text sizes, roles, weights, tracking | `src/lib/styles/typography.css` | Typography primitives, roles, and modifiers. |
55	| Borders, elevation, focus rings | `src/lib/styles/border-elevation-focus.css` | The partition-law border set and the shadow ladder. |
56	| Page frames, headers, sidebars, rails | `src/lib/styles/layout-shell.css` | Application shell hierarchy. |
57	| Colors, semantic tokens, dark mode | `src/lib/styles/colors-themes.css` | Design token source of truth. |
58	| Motion, keyframes | `src/lib/styles/motion-animation.css` | Easings, durations and animations. |
59	| Buttons, links, tags, avatars, switches | `src/lib/styles/components.css` | The interactive elements. |

69	3. If genuine new utility or shell class is required, add it to the designated stylesheet in `src/lib/styles` and run `pnpm registry`.

#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// fractalstyler lint — the design system contract linter & agent guard.
//
// Verifies code against the styling system contract:
//   - Svelte files: no scoped <style>, no style="..." attributes, all classes verified
//   - Stylesheets: token purity (no raw hex, >2px budget, valid var(--tokens))
//   - Sass files: valid interpolation, radius ladder usage
//
// Supports:
//   Self mode:     node lint/cli.ts               (inside fractalstyler repo)
//   Consumer mode: node lint/cli.ts <dir>         (linting any project using fractalstyler)
//   Flags:         --json (agent/CI output), --own <file>, --registry <file>
//
// Source is TypeScript, run directly on Node 24 in the repo; the published
// package ships the lint/cli.mjs that `pnpm build:runtime` emits next to it.
// =============================================================================

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { loadRegistry } from './lib/registry.ts';
import { lintSvelteFile } from './lib/svelte-linter.ts';
import { TokenLinter } from './lib/token-linter.ts';
import { lintHardcodedRadius, lintSassNesting } from './lib/css-linter.ts';
import { reportDiagnostics, type Diagnostic } from './lib/agent-reporter.ts';

const PKG_ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');

function usage() {
	console.log(`Usage:
  fractalstyler lint              # self mode: audit fractalstyler package
  fractalstyler lint <dir>        # consumer mode: audit project directory
Options:
  --own <file>    extension stylesheet (default <dir>/src/lib/styles/custom.css)
  --registry <f>  registry.json override
  --json          machine-readable JSON diagnostics for agents and CI
  --help          show this help message`);
}

interface Flags {
	json: boolean;
	own: string | null;
	registry: string | null;
}

const SVELTE = /\.svelte$/;
const STYLESHEET = /\.(sass|scss|css)$/;

function walk(
	dir: string,
	filter: (name: string) => boolean,
	out: string[] = [],
	base = dir,
	skip: (relativePath: string) => boolean = () => false,
	root = dir
): string[] {
	if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return out;
	for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
		if (
			entry.name === 'node_modules' ||
			entry.name === '.svelte-kit' ||
			entry.name === 'dist' ||
			entry.name === '.git' ||
			entry.name === 'reserve' ||
			entry.name.startsWith('.')
		)
			continue;

		const full = path.join(base, entry.name);
		if (skip(path.relative(root, full))) continue;
		if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(full, filter, out, full, skip, root);
		else if (filter(entry.name)) out.push(full);
	}
	return out;
}

const rel = (root: string, file: string) => path.relative(root, file);

function harvestOwnClasses(content: string): Set<string> {
	const names = new Set<string>();
	for (const m of content.matchAll(/(?:^|[\s,{}])(\.)([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)/g)) {
		names.add(m[2]);
	}
	return names;
}

async function main() {
	const args = process.argv.slice(2);
	const flags: Flags = { json: false, own: null, registry: null };
	const positional: string[] = [];

	for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
		const arg = args[i];
		if (arg === '--help' || arg === '-h') {
			usage();
			process.exit(0);
		} else if (arg === '--json') {
			flags.json = true;
		} else if (arg === '--own' && i + 1 < args.length) {
			flags.own = args[++i];
		} else if (arg === '--registry' && i + 1 < args.length) {
			flags.registry = args[++i];
		} else if (!arg.startsWith('-')) {
			positional.push(arg);
		}
	}

	const targetDir = positional[0] === 'lint' ? positional[1] : positional[0];

	let diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
	try {
		if (!targetDir || targetDir === '.') {
			diagnostics = await lintSelf(flags);
		} else {
			diagnostics = await lintConsumer(targetDir, flags);
		}

		reportDiagnostics(diagnostics, { json: flags.json });
		const hasErrors = diagnostics.some((d) => d.severity === 'error');
		process.exit(hasErrors ? 1 : 0);
	} catch (err) {
		console.error(`\x1b[31mError during lint: ${(err as Error).message}\x1b[0m`);
		if (process.env.DEBUG) console.error(err);
		process.exit(2);
	}
}

232	/** The radius ladder: a literal corner cannot be reached by the shape axis. */
233	export function lintHardcodedRadius(relPath: string, content: string): Diagnostic[] {
234		const diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
235		content.split('\n').forEach((line, idx) => {

244			if (bad.length === 0) return;
245

248				severity: 'warning',
249				file: relPath,

253				rationale:

256			});

258		return diagnostics;
259	}

261	/** `&` in a plain CSS selector — the rule never reaches the browser. */
262	export function lintSassNesting(relPath: string, content: string): Diagnostic[] {

277			});
278		});
279		return diagnostics;

### 🤖 Assistant · 2026-11-12 06:04:12

Everything is in motion; I'm now waiting on the builders, and will integrate as each reports back.

**Where it stands**
- **Project**: `packages/maxima-ui` is scaffolded on SvelteKit 3.2, Svelte 5.57 and TypeScript 6, and registered in the workspace `AGENTS.md`.
- **Styling**: a 332-line extension layer sits on top of fractalstyler through its sanctioned `custom.css` extension point. It and the Button exemplar pass fractalstyler's own linter with zero violations.
- **Motion engine**: done. One spring solver produces both the CSS `linear()` spring tokens and the JavaScript engine, so a CSS transition and a dragged element settle the same way.
- **Themes**: one parametric theme driven by three numbers (hue, chroma, tint), plus independent radius, density and motion axes.
- **Contract**: a component is a folder (source, `doc.ts`, runnable examples), and its docs page is generated from that folder. A gate script fails any component with an undocumented prop, or a prop or variant value that no example shows.
- **Running now**: 15 kit agents building about 110 components (Opus on pickers, overlays, data, motion and effects; Sonnet on the standard kits; Haiku on primitives), plus one agent finishing the generator, gate and docs site.

**Things you should know**
- maxima-ui is linked to your local `../fractalstyler`, not the npm 1.6.0 release, because the published registry lacks 52 classes the local one has (`.sr-only`, `.card`, `.field`, `.collapse`, `.btn-icon` and others). Nothing in `../fractalstyler` is edited.
- The published fractalstyler 1.6.0 lint CLI crashes when run from `node_modules` on Node 26 (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`). It works through the link.
- Adding maxima-ui to `ars-docs/.../project-tracker.json` (a fractalstyler house rule) was blocked by the permission system because the file is outside this workspace. That entry is still missing.

Next: integrate as kits land, run the full check and build, review the docs site in the browser, and send Haiku sweeps after any remaining gate failures.

This file is the **contract**. Every rule below is enforced by a script
(`pnpm gate`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`). If a rule and a script disagree, the
script is the truth — fix the file, never the gate.

## 0. Commands

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm dev` | the docs site (every component page is generated from the component folder) |
| `pnpm gen` | regenerate everything generated: `custom.css`, spring tokens, the barrel, `api.json` |
| `pnpm verify <kit>/<name>` | gen + gate + lint + type-check for ONE component — run this before you say "done" |
| `pnpm verify <kit>` | the same, for a whole kit |
| `pnpm gate` | the component↔docs contract for the whole library |
| `pnpm lint` | the fractalstyler closed-world linter |
| `pnpm check` | gen + svelte-check + lint + gate (the whole tree) |
| `pnpm build` | docs site + the publishable package |

Node 26, pnpm 11, Svelte 5.57 (runes only), SvelteKit 3, TypeScript 6 strict.

## 1. The two laws

### Law 1 — fractalstyler only

Styling is **composition of registered classes in markup**. Nothing else.

- NO `<style>` blocks. NO `style="…"`. NO `style:prop` directives.
- NO raw hex colours, NO pixel literals above 2px, NO literal `border-radius`.
- NO inline `<svg>` and NO unicode glyph icons — icons are
  `import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons'` +
  `import { luCheck } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide'` → `<Icon icon={luCheck} />`.
  (Check a name exists: `grep -c "luName\b" node_modules/@fractaldesign/icons/dist/lucide.d.ts`.)
- Every class must exist in **fractalstyler's registry**
  (`node_modules/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/registry.md` — read it) or in the
  **maxima extension layer** (`src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` — read them; they
  are short).
- Modifiers are never standalone: `.row.xcenter`, never a bare `.xcenter`.
- There is no `.w-*`, `.pad-x-*`, `.border-top`. Search the registry; never guess.

**Dynamic values travel through custom properties.** JavaScript may write
*only* custom properties — `node.style.setProperty('--x', …)` — and a class
owns the real property (`translate: calc(var(--mx, 0) * 1px) …`). Use the
`vars()` attachment (`src/lib/motion`) to bind values:
`<div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: 0.4 })}>`. Never assign
`node.style.transform = …` or any real property.

**The extension layer is small on purpose.** Compose first. If the system
genuinely cannot express something, add the *smallest general primitive* to
your kit's fragment `src/lib/styles/layers/kits/<kit>.css`:

- plain CSS, tokens only (`var(--space-*)`, `var(--radius-*)`, colour roles),
  `rem`/`em`/`%` — no px above 2, no hex, no `&` nesting;
- named in the system's voice (`.track`, `.thumb`, `.indicator`) — a
  primitive several components could use, not `.my-component-inner`;
- hard budget: **90 lines per kit fragment**. The gate fails above it;
- only edit your own kit's fragment. Never edit `custom.css` (generated) or
  another layer file. After editing run `pnpm gen`.

### Law 2 — a component and its documentation are one

A component is a **folder**. It is not done until the folder passes
`pnpm verify <kit>/<name>`:

```
src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/        # <name> is kebab-case
  <Name>.svelte                         # the primary component (PascalCase of <name>)
  <NamePart>.svelte …                   # optional further parts (DialogTitle.svelte)
  <name>.svelte.ts | <name>.ts          # optional logic/state modules
  index.ts                              # named exports of every public thing
  doc.ts                                # the documentation manifest
  examples/01-usage.svelte              # ≥ 1, ordered by numeric prefix
  examples/02-….svelte
```

The docs page is **generated** from that folder — you never write a route:

- **Install / import** — generated from the package name and `index.ts`.
- **Examples** — each example file is rendered live *and* shown as source
  (the same file, so demo and code cannot drift).
- **API tables** — extracted from each part's `interface Props` and its JSDoc.
- **Accessibility / keyboard** — from `doc.ts`.

What the gate requires:

1. `index.ts` exports the primary component and every part
   (`export { default as Button } from './Button.svelte';`).
2. Every exported `.svelte` part declares `interface Props` in its instance
   script. **Every prop has a JSDoc comment** (one sentence or more). Defaults
   are documented by the destructuring default or an explicit `@default` tag.
3. `doc.ts` default-exports `defineDoc({...})` (shape below), nothing empty.
4. Each example starts with the header line
   `<!-- @example Title :: One sentence describing what it shows. -->`
   and example 01 is the minimal usage.
5. **Coverage — nothing is left out.** Across the folder's examples:
   every value of every string-literal-union prop (`variant`, `size`, `shape`,
   `placement`, …) appears; every prop name declared in `Props` (of every part)
   appears. (`class`, `children`, `ref` are exempt.)
6. Law 1, statically: no style blocks/attributes/directives, no `<svg`, no
   `.style.` writes other than `setProperty('--…')`, and every class token in a
   `class="…"` / `class={…}` literal is registered.
7. Inside `src/lib`, imports are **relative** (no `#lib`, no `$lib`). Examples
   import only from `@fractaldesign/maxima-ui` (and `/motion`, `/theme`),
   `@fractaldesign/icons*`, and `svelte*` — exactly what a consumer would write.

### `doc.ts`

```ts
import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',                       // the primary export
	summary: 'One sentence. Shown in the index and the page header.',
	description: `One to three paragraphs. Blank line = new paragraph. \`code\` allowed.`,
	parts: { ButtonGroup: 'One line: what this part is for.' },   // optional, every non-primary .svelte export
	features: ['Spring-pressed', '…'],    // optional bullets
	accessibility: ['Renders a native <button> …'],               // ≥ 1
	keyboard: [{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' }],   // when interactive
	api: [{ name: 'toast(message, options?)', type: '(…) => string', description: '…' }], // non-component exports
	related: ['icon-button']              // optional slugs
});
```

## 2. Authoring conventions

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { sizeClass, type Size, type Shape, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style of the button. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The content. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let { variant = 'primary', size = 'md', class: klass, children, ...rest }: Props = $props();
</script>

<button class={['button', variant, sizeClass[size], klass]} {...rest}>
	{@render children?.()}
</button>
```

- Runes only: `$props`, `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$bindable`,
  `$props.id()` for ids. Snippets, never slots. `{@attach}`, never `use:`.
  Callback props (`onchange`), never `createEventDispatcher`.
- `class` is always accepted and merged last via the array form
  `class={['…', cond && '…', klass]}`. Spread `...rest` onto the root element
  and extend the matching `svelte/elements` attribute type.
- Two-way state is `$bindable()` **and** has a callback
  (`value = $bindable()`, `onValueChange`). Works controlled and uncontrolled.
- Shared axes come from `src/lib/internal/tokens.ts` — do not redefine:
  `Variant` (`primary secondary themed outline ghost link soft info success
  warning danger`), `Size` (`xs sm md lg xl` → `sizeClass[size]`), `Shape`
  (`rect mincurved modern curved round`), `Tone` (`neutral info success
  warning danger`), `Placement`.
- Compound components share state with `createContext` from `svelte`
  (`const [getTabs, setTabs] = createContext<TabsState>()`).
- Use the platform first: native `<dialog>`, the Popover API (`popover`
  attribute), CSS anchor positioning (`.anchor` / `.floating`, see
  `src/lib/internal/floating.ts`), `<details>`, `:has()`, `@starting-style`
  enter/exit (`.pop` + `.enter-*`). JavaScript only where the platform stops.
- SSR-safe: no `window`/`document` at module or init time — only inside
  `$effect`, attachments and event handlers.
- Accessible by construction: correct roles, `aria-*` wiring, labels, focus
  management, full keyboard support (document it in `doc.ts`).
- Motion (all from `src/lib/motion`): springs for anything a user moves or
  triggers; honour reduced motion (the motion layer already does — do not
  bypass it). Prefer CSS spring tokens (`.spring.snappy`, `.pop`) for
  state-driven motion; the JS spring engine (`animate`, `SpringValue`, the
  attachments) for gestures and layout.
- No new dependencies. No `any`. No `@ts-ignore`. No TODOs.
- Aesthetic bar: restrained, precise, premium. Hairline borders, the
  elevation ladder, generous but consistent spacing from the space ladder,
  `text-secondary`/`text-muted` for hierarchy, `.rim` + `.shad-*` on raised
  surfaces, `.glass` on floating ones, tabular numerals for numbers. Examples
  use realistic content (real product copy, never "foo"/"Lorem ipsum").

## 3. Map

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` | the maxima extension layer — sources. `kits/<kit>.css` are the kit fragments |
| `src/lib/styles/custom.css` | GENERATED concat of the layers — fractalstyler's sanctioned `custom.css` extension point; the linter reads it |
| `src/lib/internal/` | shared tokens, floating/anchor helpers, list navigation, highlight |
| `src/lib/motion/` | spring solver, CSS spring tokens, `animate`, attachments, transitions, view transitions |
| `src/lib/theme/` | parametric theme runtime (mode, theme, hue/chroma, radius, density, motion) |
| `src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/` | the components — see Law 2 |
| `src/lib/components/kits.ts` | the kit list (order, titles) |
| `src/lib/docs/` | `defineDoc`, doc types, GENERATED `api.json` |
| `src/lib/index.ts` | GENERATED barrel |
| `src/routes/` | the docs site — generated pages + hand-written guides |
| `scripts/` | `gen.ts`, `gate.ts`, `verify.ts` and friends |

Generated files carry a `GENERATED` banner — never edit them by hand.

## 4. House rules

- fractalstyler is consumed from `../fractalstyler` (linked). **Never edit
  anything in `../fractalstyler`.** Missing primitives go in the extension layer.
- Do not initialise git, commit, push or publish unless the user asks.
- Work only in the paths you were assigned; other agents are working in
  parallel in sibling folders. Never "fix" a sibling's files — report instead.

## 5. Motion and theme quick reference

Import inside `src/lib` from `'../../../motion/index.js'` / `'../../../theme/index.js'`;
in examples from `'@fractaldesign/maxima-ui/motion'` / `'/theme'` (also re-exported
from the root). Read the sources for the full JSDoc.

```ts
// springs — presets: 'gentle' | 'snappy' | 'bouncy' | 'stiff' | 'slow', or { stiffness, damping, mass }
springs, resolveSpring(input?), springDuration(input?), springEasing(input?), springEase(input?)

// engine — element must carry class "motion" (x y scale rotate opacity) or "tilt" (rotateX rotateY)
animate(node, { x, y, scale, rotate, opacity, rotateX, rotateY, '--custom': n }, { spring, instant, onUpdate }) → { finished, stop() }
setMotion(node, values)   getMotion(node, channel)
new SpringValue(initial, spring?)  → .current (reactive) .target .set(v, { instant })
reducedMotion.current

// attachments — {@attach name(options)}
vars({ value: 0.4 })                    // writes --value (any custom properties)
press() hover() magnetic() tilt()       // interaction springs
pointer()                               // writes --px/--py for spotlights
inView({ class: 'in' }) reveal() stagger()   // entrance; stagger writes --i on children
drag({ axis, bounds, snapBack, momentum, onDragEnd })
parallax() scrollProgress()
createFlip() → { attach, read(), play(), run(fn) }   // FLIP layout springs; items carry data-flip-id

// Svelte transitions with spring easing — transition:springScale={{ spring: 'bouncy' }}
springFade springFly springScale springBlur springSlide

// view transitions
startViewTransition(update, { type: 'fade'|'slide'|'slide-back'|'scale'|'reveal'|'none', origin })
setupViewTransitions(onNavigate, { type })    vtName('hero')   // element also needs class "vt-name"

// theme
theme (ThemeState: mode theme hue chroma tint radius density motion resolvedMode; setTheme() setMode() toggleMode(event) reset())
themes, initTheme(), themeInitScript()
```

CSS side (see `src/lib/styles/layers/10-motion.css`): `.spring` + `.spring-<preset>`
for state transitions, `.pop` + `.enter-*` for anything that opens (works on
`[popover]`, `<dialog open>`, and `.open`), `.anim-in` (staggered by `--i`),
`.reveal`/`.in`, `.lift`, `.press`.

# DESIGN

The design language of maxima-ui. It is fractalstyler's language, held to a
premium bar — restrained, precise, quiet until touched.

## Principles

1. **Composition over invention.** A component is a sentence written in
   fractalstyler's vocabulary. If two components look related, it is because
   they share classes, not because someone matched them by eye.
2. **Hierarchy through ink, not size.** `text-primary` → `text-secondary` →
   `text-muted` carry most hierarchy. Size and weight change rarely.
3. **Hairlines and light.** Surfaces are separated by 1px borders
   (`border`, `border-subtle`) and lifted by the elevation ladder (`shad-*`)
   with a lit top edge (`rim`). Floating surfaces are `glass`.
4. **Motion is physics.** Anything a person moves or triggers is driven by a
   spring — the same solver produces the CSS `linear()` tokens
   (`--spring-snappy` …) and drives the JavaScript engine, so a CSS transition
   and a dragged element settle the same way. Motion is interruptible, never
   blocks input, and collapses to nothing under reduced motion.
5. **One theme, three numbers.** `--hue`, `--chroma`, `--tint` generate every
   colour role in both modes. Shape (`data-radius`), density (`data-density`)
   and motion (`data-motion`) are independent axes that rewrite ladders, not
   components.

## The shared axes

| Axis | Values | Mechanism |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `variant` | primary · secondary · themed · soft · outline · ghost · link · info · success · warning · danger | a class of the same name |
| `size` | xs · sm · md · lg · xl | `sizeClass[size]` → height + text ladder |
| `shape` | rect · mincurved · modern · curved · round | a class of the same name |
| `tone` | neutral · info · success · warning · danger | status colour roles |

## The extension layer

| Layer | Adds |
|:---|:---|
| `00-tokens` | motion channels (`@property`), spring/motion scale, measure ladder |
| `01-springs` | generated `--spring-*` `linear()` easings |
| `10-motion` | `.motion` `.tilt` `.spring` `.pop` `.enter-*` `.anim-*` `.reveal`, view transitions |
| `20-surface` | `.glass` `.rim` `.glow` `.soft` `.measure-*` and small layout primitives |
| `30-overlay` | `.anchor` `.floating` `.dialog` `.sheet` `.layer` |
| `40-controls` | `.bare` `.item` `.track` `.fill` `.thumb` `.ring` `.indicator` `.caret` |
| `60-themes` | the parametric theme and the radius / density / motion axes |
| `kits/*` | ≤ 90 lines per kit, for primitives composition cannot express |

=== src/lib/components/actions/button/Button.svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLAnchorAttributes, HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons';
	import type { IconData } from '@fractaldesign/icons';
	import { luLoaderCircle } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide';
	import { press } from '../../../motion/index.js';
	import { sizeClass, type Shape, type Size, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style. `primary` is the page's main action; use one per view. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The corner shape. */
		shape?: Shape;
		/** An icon drawn before the label. */
		icon?: IconData;
		/** An icon drawn after the label. */
		iconEnd?: IconData;
		/** Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and blocks interaction, keeping the button's width. */
		loading?: boolean;
		/** Stretches the button to the full width of its container. */
		block?: boolean;
		/** Renders an `<a>` that looks like a button. Use for navigation. */
		href?: string;
		/** Where to open the link, when `href` is set. */
		target?: HTMLAnchorAttributes['target'];
		/** Springs the button down under the pointer. Turn off for a still button. */
		pressable?: boolean;
		/** The label. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let {
		variant = 'primary',
		size = 'md',
		shape = 'modern',
		icon,
		iconEnd,
		loading = false,
		block = false,
		href,
		target,
		pressable = true,
		disabled,
		type = 'button',
		class: klass,
		children,
		...rest
	}: Props = $props();

	const classes = $derived([
		'button no-scaling gap-sm weight-500',
		variant,
		sizeClass[size],
		shape,
		block ? 'wfull' : 'inline-flex',
		pressable && 'motion',
		klass
	]);
	const spring = $derived(pressable ? press() : undefined);
</script>

{#snippet content()}
	{#if loading}
		<Icon icon={luLoaderCircle} class="anim-spin" />
	{:else if icon}
		<Icon {icon} />
	{/if}
	{@render children?.()}
	{#if iconEnd}
		<Icon icon={iconEnd} />
	{/if}
{/snippet}

{#if href && !disabled}
	<a
		class={classes}
		{href}
		{target}
		rel={target === '_blank' ? 'noopener noreferrer' : undefined}
		aria-busy={loading || undefined}
		{@attach spring}
		{...rest as HTMLAnchorAttributes}
	>
		{@render content()}
	</a>
{:else}
	<button
		class={classes}
		{type}
		disabled={disabled || loading}
		aria-busy={loading || undefined}
		{@attach spring}
		{...rest}
	>
		{@render content()}
	</button>
{/if}

import type { Attachment } from 'svelte/attachments';

/** The CSS anchor name for an id — `$props.id()` output is a fine id. */
export function anchorName(id: string): string {
	return `--anchor-${id.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '')}`;
}

/**
 * Pair a trigger with its floating element. Put `{@attach anchor(id)}` on the
 * trigger (with class `anchor`) and `{@attach floating(id)}` on the floating
 * element (with class `floating at-…`): both receive the same `--anchor`
 * name, and CSS anchor positioning does the rest.
 */
export function anchor(id: string): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		node.style.setProperty('--anchor', anchorName(id));
		return () => node.style.removeProperty('--anchor');
	};
}

/** The floating side of `anchor()`. `offset` overrides the gap (any CSS length or token). */
export function floating(id: string, offset?: string): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		node.style.setProperty('--anchor', anchorName(id));
		if (offset) node.style.setProperty('--offset', offset);
		return () => {
			node.style.removeProperty('--anchor');
			node.style.removeProperty('--offset');
		};
	};
}

/**
 * Keep a boolean in step with a native popover element.
 * Returns an attachment for the `[popover]` element: it shows/hides the
 * popover when `isOpen()` changes and reports user dismissal through `onChange`.
 */
export function popoverSync(
	isOpen: () => boolean,
	onChange: (open: boolean) => void

	return (node) => {
		const want = isOpen();
		const shown = node.matches(':popover-open');
		if (want && !shown) node.showPopover();
		else if (!want && shown) node.hidePopover();

		};

.field > .input:focus-visible, .field > [role='combobox']:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: none; }

export function loadAllowlist(layers: LayerBuild): Allowlist {

export function checkScriptAst(code: string, file: string, lineBase: number, inMotion: boolean): Diag[] {

export function checkKitFragments(layers: LayerBuild, kits: KitInfo[], onlyKit: string | null): Diag[] {
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	for (const fl of layers.files) {
		if (!fl.name.startsWith('kits/')) continue;
		const kit = fl.name.slice(5).replace(/\.css$/, '');
		if (onlyKit && kit !== onlyKit) continue;
		const file = rel(fl.full);
		const n = cssCodeLines(fl.source);
		if (n > KIT_BUDGET)
			out.push({ rule: 'layer/budget', severity: 'error', file, line: null, message: `${n} lines (budget ${KIT_BUDGET})`, fix: 'compose more in markup; keep only the smallest general primitives' });
		if (!kits.some((k) => k.id === kit))
			out.push({ rule: 'kit/unknown', severity: 'error', file, line: null, message: `kit fragment for unknown kit "${kit}"`, fix: 'name the fragment after a kit in kits.ts' });
		for (const m of fl.source.matchAll(/&/g)) {
			out.push({ rule: 'layer/nesting', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(fl.source, m.index ?? 0), message: '`&` nesting in a plain CSS layer', fix: 'write the selector out in full' });
			break;
		}
	}
	return out;
}

/** Law 1 + imports for src/lib outside the component folders. */
export function checkLibraryFiles(allow: Allowlist): Diag[] {
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	const files = walkFiles(PATHS.lib, (n) => n.endsWith('.ts') || n.endsWith('.svelte')).filter((full) => {
		const r = rel(full);
		return !r.startsWith('src/lib/components/') && !r.startsWith('src/lib/docs/generated/') && r !== 'src/lib/index.ts';
	});
	for (const full of files) out.push(...checkFile(full, allow));
	out.push(...checkTokenMaps(allow));
	return out;
}

export function vars(values: Record<string, string | number | null | undefined>): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		const written: string[] = [];
		for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(values)) {
			const prop = key.startsWith('--') ? key : `--${key}`;
			if (value === null || value === undefined || (typeof value === 'number' && !Number.isFinite(value))) {
				node.style.removeProperty(prop);
				continue;
			}
			node.style.setProperty(prop, typeof value === 'number' ? fmt(value) : value);
			written.push(prop);
		}
		return () => {
			for (const prop of written) node.style.removeProperty(prop);
		};
	};
}

			from: before.get(id),
			last: el.getBoundingClientRect(),
			x: getMotion(el, 'x'),
			y: getMotion(el, 'y'),
			s: getMotion(el, 'scale'),
			vx: getVelocity(el, 'x'),
			vy: getVelocity(el, 'y'),
			vs: getVelocity(el, 'scale')
		}));
		// Write phase.
		for (const p of plans) {
			if (!p.from) {
				if (before.size > 0) {
					setMotion(p.el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.96 });
					animate(p.el, { opacity: 1, scale: 1 }, { spring });
				}
				continue;
			}
			const dx = p.from.left + p.from.width / 2 - (p.last.left + p.last.width / 2);
			const dy = p.from.top + p.from.height / 2 - (p.last.top + p.last.height / 2);
			let s = p.s;
			if (p.last.width > 0 && p.last.height > 0) {
				const ws = p.from.width / p.last.width;
				const hs = p.from.height / p.last.height;
				if (Math.abs(ws - hs) <= 0.05 * Math.max(ws, hs)) s = p.s * Math.sqrt(ws * hs);
			}
			if (Math.abs(dx) < 0.5 && Math.abs(dy) < 0.5 && Math.abs(s - p.s) < 0.001) continue;
			setMotion(p.el, { x: p.x + dx, y: p.y + dy, scale: s });
			animate(p.el, { x: 0, y: 0, scale: 1 }, { spring, velocity: { x: p.vx, y: p.vy, scale: p.vs } });
		}
	};

	return {
		attach: (node) => {
			container = node;
			return () => {
				if (container === node) container = null;
				first = new Map();
			};
		},
		read,
		play,
		async run(fn) {
			read();
			await fn();
			await tick();
			play();
		}
	};
}

function memberName(m: ts.TypeElement, sf: ts.SourceFile): string | null {
	if (!m.name) return null;
	if (ts.isIdentifier(m.name) || ts.isStringLiteral(m.name)) return m.name.text;
	return m.name.getText(sf);
}

interface Destructured {
	default: string | null;
	bindable: boolean;
}

function findPropsDestructuring(sf: ts.SourceFile): Map<string, Destructured> {
	const out = new Map<string, Destructured>();
	const visit = (n: ts.Node) => {
		if (
			ts.isVariableDeclaration(n) &&
			n.initializer &&
			ts.isCallExpression(n.initializer) &&
			n.initializer.expression.getText(sf) === '$props' &&
			ts.isObjectBindingPattern(n.name)
		) {
			for (const el of n.name.elements) {
				if (el.dotDotDotToken) continue;
				const key = el.propertyName
					? ts.isIdentifier(el.propertyName) || ts.isStringLiteral(el.propertyName)
						? el.propertyName.text
						: el.propertyName.getText(sf)
					: ts.isIdentifier(el.name)
						? el.name.text
						: null;
				if (!key) continue;
				const init = el.initializer;
				if (init && ts.isCallExpression(init) && init.expression.getText(sf) === '$bindable') {
					out.set(key, { bindable: true, default: init.arguments[0] ? norm(init.arguments[0].getText(sf)) : null });
				} else {
					out.set(key, { bindable: false, default: init ? norm(init.getText(sf)) : null });
				}
			}
			return;
		}
		ts.forEachChild(n, visit);
	};
	visit(sf);
	return out;
}

/** Exported type aliases of every plain .ts module in the component folder. */
export function folderAliases(dir: string): Aliases {
	const aliases: Aliases = new Map();
	for (const name of listDir(dir, 'file')) {
		if (!name.endsWith('.ts') || name === 'doc.ts') continue;
		collectAliases(parseTs(readText(path.join(dir, name)) ?? '', name), true, aliases);
	}
	return aliases;
}

export function analyzePart(name: string, file: string, src: string, folderTypes: Aliases): PartInfo {
	const part: PartInfo = { name, file, inherits: [], props: [], hasProps: false, propsLine: 1, problems: [] };
	const scripts = extractScripts(src);
	const instance = scripts.find((s) => !s.module);
	const moduleScript = scripts.find((s) => s.module);
	if (!instance) {
		part.problems.push('no instance <script lang="ts">');
		return part;
	}
	const sf = parseTs(instance.content, file + '.ts');
	const msf = moduleScript ? parseTs(moduleScript.content, file + '.module.ts') : null;
	const local: Aliases = collectAliases(sf, false);
	if (msf) collectAliases(msf, false, local);
	const aliasChain = [local, folderTypes, tokenAliases()];

	let found = findProps(sf);
	let foundIn = sf;
	let foundLine = instance.line;
	if (!found && msf && moduleScript) {
		found = findProps(msf);
		foundIn = msf;
		foundLine = moduleScript.line;
	}
	if (!found) return part;

	part.hasProps = true;
	part.inherits = found.inherits;
	part.propsLine = foundLine + foundIn.getLineAndCharacterOfPosition(found.node.getStart(foundIn)).line;
	const destructured = findPropsDestructuring(sf);

	for (const m of found.members) {
		const pname = memberName(m, foundIn);
		if (!pname) continue;
		let typeText = 'unknown';
		let typeNode: ts.TypeNode | undefined;
		if (ts.isPropertySignature(m) && m.type) {
			typeNode = m.type;
			typeText = norm(m.type.getText(foundIn));
		} else if (ts.isMethodSignature(m)) {
			const params = m.parameters.map((p) => norm(p.getText(foundIn))).join(', ');
			typeText = `(${params}) => ${m.type ? norm(m.type.getText(foundIn)) : 'void'}`;
		}
		const { description, defaultTag } = jsdocOf(m, foundIn);
		const d = destructured.get(pname);
		part.props.push({
			name: pname,
			type: typeText,
			resolvedValues: resolveLiterals(typeNode, aliasChain),
			optional: Boolean(m.questionToken),
			bindable: d?.bindable ?? false,
			default: defaultTag ?? d?.default ?? null,
			description,
			snippet: /^Snippet\b/.test(typeText),
			line: foundLine + foundIn.getLineAndCharacterOfPosition(m.getStart(foundIn)).line
		});
	}
	return part;
}

export function toApiPart(p: PartInfo): ApiPart {
	return {
		name: p.name,
		file: p.file,
		inherits: p.inherits,
		props: p.props.map(({ line: _line, ...rest }) => rest)
	};
}

/**
 * A reactive, spring-driven number. Setting `target` animates `current`
 * along the spring; reading `current` in a template or `$derived` re-renders
 * every frame while it moves. Retargeting mid-flight keeps the velocity, so
 * motion stays continuous. Shares the motion layer's single rAF loop and
 * honours reduced motion (jumps to the target). SSR-safe.
 *
 * @example
 * ```svelte
 * <script lang="ts">
 * 	import { SpringValue, vars } from '@fractaldesign/maxima-ui/motion';
 * 	const width = new SpringValue(0, 'gentle');
 * </script>
 * <div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: width.current })}></div>
 * <button onclick={() => (width.target = 0.8)}>Grow</button>
 * ```
 */
export class SpringValue {
	#current = $state(0);
	#target = $state(0);
	#state: SpringState = { x: 0, v: 0 };
	#precision = 0.001;
	#running = false;
	#waiters: (() => void)[] = [];

	/** The spring used for subsequent motion (preset name or partial config). */
	spring: SpringInput;

	/**
	 * @param initial The starting value (also the initial target).
	 * @param spring The spring to use. Defaults to `'snappy'`.
	 */
	constructor(initial: number, spring: SpringInput = 'snappy') {
		this.#current = initial;
		this.#target = initial;
		this.#state.x = initial;
		this.spring = spring;
	}

	/** The current animated value (reactive, read-only — set `target` or call `set()`). */
	get current(): number {
		return this.#current;
	}

	/** The value being animated toward (reactive). Assigning it starts the spring. */
	get target(): number {
		return this.#target;
	}

	set target(value: number) {
		void this.set(value);
	}

	/** The current velocity in units per second. Assign to impart momentum. */
	get velocity(): number {
		return this.#state.v;
	}

	set velocity(value: number) {
		this.#state.v = Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Animate to `value`. Resolves when the spring settles (or is stopped or jumped).
	 * @param value The new target.
	 * @param opts `instant` jumps with no animation; `velocity` sets the starting velocity (units/s).
	 */
	set(value: number, opts: { instant?: boolean; velocity?: number } = {}): Promise<void> {
		if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return Promise.resolve();
		this.#target = value;

/** Exactly the regex fractalstyler's `lint` uses on a consumer's custom.css. */
export function harvestLikeLinter(css: string): Set<string> {
	const names = new Set<string>();
	for (const m of css.matchAll(/(?:^|[\s,{}])(\.)([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)/g)) names.add(m[2]);
	return names;
}

/** Map a line of the generated custom.css back to its layer file. */
export function mapCustomLine(segments: LayerSegment[], line: number): { file: string; line: number } | null {
	for (const s of segments) {
		if (line >= s.start && line < s.start + s.lines) return { file: s.file, line: line - s.start + 1 };
	}
	return null;
}

// ── parser ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function stripComments(src: string): string {
	return src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, (m) => blank(m));
}

function skipString(src: string, i: number): number {
	const q = src[i];
	let j = i + 1;
	while (j < src.length && src[j] !== q) {
		if (src[j] === '\\') j++;
		j++;
	}
	return j;
}

function matchBrace(src: string, open: number): number {
	let depth = 0;
	for (let i = open; i < src.length; i++) {
		const c = src[i];
		if (c === '"' || c === "'") i = skipString(src, i);
		else if (c === '{') depth++;
		else if (c === '}') {
			depth--;
			if (depth === 0) return i;
		}
	}
	return src.length;
}

function parseBlock(src: string, from: number, to: number, full: string): { rules: CssRule[]; decls: string[] } {
	const rules: CssRule[] = [];
	const decls: string[] = [];
	let seg = from;
	let paren = 0;
	for (let i = from; i < to; i++) {
		const c = src[i];
		if (c === '"' || c === "'") {
			i = skipString(src, i);
		} else if (c === '(') paren++;
		else if (c === ')') paren = Math.max(0, paren - 1);
		else if (c === ';' && paren === 0) {
			const d = src.slice(seg, i).trim();
			if (d) {
				// `@import …;` and friends at block level are statements, not declarations.
				if (!d.startsWith('@')) decls.push(d.replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
			}
			seg = i + 1;
		} else if (c === '{' && paren === 0) {
			const close = matchBrace(src, i);
			const prelude = src.slice(seg, i).trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
			const inner = parseBlock(src, i + 1, Math.min(close, to), full);
			rules.push({ prelude, declarations: inner.decls, children: inner.rules, line: lineAt(full, seg + (src.slice(seg, i).length - src.slice(seg, i).trimStart().length)) });
			i = close;
			seg = close + 1;
		}
	}
	const tail = src.slice(seg, to).trim();
	if (tail && !tail.startsWith('@')) decls.push(tail.replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
	return { rules, decls };
}

export function parseCss(source: string): CssRule[] {
	const src = stripComments(source);
	return parseBlock(src, 0, src.length, source).rules;
}

const SKIP_AT = /^@(keyframes|-webkit-keyframes|font-face|property|counter-style|page|font-feature-values)\b/;

function harvestRuleClasses(file: string, source: string): ClassEntry[] {
	const out: ClassEntry[] = [];
	const visit = (rules: CssRule[]) => {
		for (const r of rules) {
			if (r.prelude.startsWith('@')) {
				if (!SKIP_AT.test(r.prelude)) visit(r.children);
				continue;
			}
			const names = new Set<string>();
			for (const m of r.prelude.matchAll(/\.(-?[a-zA-Z_][\w-]*)/g)) names.add(m[1]);
			for (const name of names) {
				out.push({ class: name, file, selector: r.prelude, declarations: r.declarations.join('; ') });
			}
			visit(r.children);
		}
	};
	visit(parseCss(source));
	return out;
}

This file is the **contract**. Every rule below is enforced by a script
(`pnpm gate`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`). If a rule and a script disagree, the
script is the truth — fix the file, never the gate.

## 0. Commands

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm dev` | the docs site (every component page is generated from the component folder) |
| `pnpm gen` | regenerate everything generated: `custom.css`, spring tokens, the barrel, `api.json` |
| `pnpm verify <kit>/<name>` | gen + gate + lint + type-check for ONE component — run this before you say "done" |
| `pnpm verify <kit>` | the same, for a whole kit |
| `pnpm gate` | the component↔docs contract for the whole library |
| `pnpm lint` | the fractalstyler closed-world linter |
| `pnpm check` | gen + svelte-check + lint + gate (the whole tree) |
| `pnpm build` | docs site + the publishable package |

Node 26, pnpm 11, Svelte 5.57 (runes only), SvelteKit 3, TypeScript 6 strict.

## 1. The two laws

### Law 1 — fractalstyler only

Styling is **composition of registered classes in markup**. Nothing else.

- NO `<style>` blocks. NO `style="…"`. NO `style:prop` directives.
- NO raw hex colours, NO pixel literals above 2px, NO literal `border-radius`.
- NO inline `<svg>` and NO unicode glyph icons — icons are
  `import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons'` +
  `import { luCheck } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide'` → `<Icon icon={luCheck} />`.
  (Check a name exists: `grep -c "luName\b" node_modules/@fractaldesign/icons/dist/lucide.d.ts`.)
- Every class must exist in **fractalstyler's registry**
  (`node_modules/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/registry.md` — read it) or in the
  **maxima extension layer** (`src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` — read them; they
  are short).
- Modifiers are never standalone: `.row.xcenter`, never a bare `.xcenter`.
- There is no `.w-*`, `.pad-x-*`, `.border-top`. Search the registry; never guess.

**Dynamic values travel through custom properties.** JavaScript may write
*only* custom properties — `node.style.setProperty('--x', …)` — and a class
owns the real property (`translate: calc(var(--mx, 0) * 1px) …`). Use the
`vars()` attachment (`src/lib/motion`) to bind values:
`<div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: 0.4 })}>`. Never assign
`node.style.transform = …` or any real property.

**The extension layer is small on purpose.** Compose first. If the system
genuinely cannot express something, add the *smallest general primitive* to
your kit's fragment `src/lib/styles/layers/kits/<kit>.css`:

- plain CSS, tokens only (`var(--space-*)`, `var(--radius-*)`, colour roles),
  `rem`/`em`/`%` — no px above 2, no hex, no `&` nesting;
- named in the system's voice (`.track`, `.thumb`, `.indicator`) — a
  primitive several components could use, not `.my-component-inner`;
- hard budget: **90 lines per kit fragment**. The gate fails above it;
- only edit your own kit's fragment. Never edit `custom.css` (generated) or
  another layer file. After editing run `pnpm gen`.

### Law 2 — a component and its documentation are one

A component is a **folder**. It is not done until the folder passes
`pnpm verify <kit>/<name>`:

```
src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/        # <name> is kebab-case
  <Name>.svelte                         # the primary component (PascalCase of <name>)
  <NamePart>.svelte …                   # optional further parts (DialogTitle.svelte)
  <name>.svelte.ts | <name>.ts          # optional logic/state modules
  index.ts                              # named exports of every public thing
  doc.ts                                # the documentation manifest
  examples/01-usage.svelte              # ≥ 1, ordered by numeric prefix
  examples/02-….svelte
```

The docs page is **generated** from that folder — you never write a route:

- **Install / import** — generated from the package name and `index.ts`.
- **Examples** — each example file is rendered live *and* shown as source
  (the same file, so demo and code cannot drift).
- **API tables** — extracted from each part's `interface Props` and its JSDoc.
- **Accessibility / keyboard** — from `doc.ts`.

What the gate requires:

1. `index.ts` exports the primary component and every part
   (`export { default as Button } from './Button.svelte';`).
2. Every exported `.svelte` part declares `interface Props` in its instance
   script. **Every prop has a JSDoc comment** (one sentence or more). Defaults
   are documented by the destructuring default or an explicit `@default` tag.
3. `doc.ts` default-exports `defineDoc({...})` (shape below), nothing empty.
4. Each example starts with the header line
   `<!-- @example Title :: One sentence describing what it shows. -->`
   and example 01 is the minimal usage.
5. **Coverage — nothing is left out.** Across the folder's examples:
   every value of every string-literal-union prop (`variant`, `size`, `shape`,
   `placement`, …) appears; every prop name declared in `Props` (of every part)
   appears. (`class`, `children`, `ref` are exempt.)
6. Law 1, statically: no style blocks/attributes/directives, no `<svg`, no
   `.style.` writes other than `setProperty('--…')`, and every class token in a
   `class="…"` / `class={…}` literal is registered.
7. Inside `src/lib`, imports are **relative** (no `#lib`, no `$lib`). Examples
   import only from `@fractaldesign/maxima-ui` (and `/motion`, `/theme`),
   `@fractaldesign/icons*`, and `svelte*` — exactly what a consumer would write.

### `doc.ts`

```ts
import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',                       // the primary export
	summary: 'One sentence. Shown in the index and the page header.',
	description: `One to three paragraphs. Blank line = new paragraph. \`code\` allowed.`,
	parts: { ButtonGroup: 'One line: what this part is for.' },   // optional, every non-primary .svelte export
	features: ['Spring-pressed', '…'],    // optional bullets
	accessibility: ['Renders a native <button> …'],               // ≥ 1
	keyboard: [{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' }],   // when interactive
	api: [{ name: 'toast(message, options?)', type: '(…) => string', description: '…' }], // non-component exports
	related: ['icon-button']              // optional slugs
});
```

## 2. Authoring conventions

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { sizeClass, type Size, type Shape, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style of the button. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The content. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let { variant = 'primary', size = 'md', class: klass, children, ...rest }: Props = $props();
</script>

<button class={['button', variant, sizeClass[size], klass]} {...rest}>
	{@render children?.()}
</button>
```

- Runes only: `$props`, `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$bindable`,
  `$props.id()` for ids. Snippets, never slots. `{@attach}`, never `use:`.
  Callback props (`onchange`), never `createEventDispatcher`.
- `class` is always accepted and merged last via the array form
  `class={['…', cond && '…', klass]}`. Spread `...rest` onto the root element
  and extend the matching `svelte/elements` attribute type.
- Two-way state is `$bindable()` **and** has a callback
  (`value = $bindable()`, `onValueChange`). Works controlled and uncontrolled.
- Shared axes come from `src/lib/internal/tokens.ts` — do not redefine:
  `Variant` (`primary secondary themed outline ghost link soft info success
  warning danger`), `Size` (`xs sm md lg xl` → `sizeClass[size]`), `Shape`
  (`rect mincurved modern curved round`), `Tone` (`neutral info success
  warning danger`), `Placement`.
- Compound components share state with `createContext` from `svelte`
  (`const [getTabs, setTabs] = createContext<TabsState>()`).
- Use the platform first: native `<dialog>`, the Popover API (`popover`
  attribute), CSS anchor positioning (`.anchor` / `.floating`, see
  `src/lib/internal/floating.ts`), `<details>`, `:has()`, `@starting-style`
  enter/exit (`.pop` + `.enter-*`). JavaScript only where the platform stops.
- SSR-safe: no `window`/`document` at module or init time — only inside
  `$effect`, attachments and event handlers.
- Accessible by construction: correct roles, `aria-*` wiring, labels, focus
  management, full keyboard support (document it in `doc.ts`).
- Motion (all from `src/lib/motion`): springs for anything a user moves or
  triggers; honour reduced motion (the motion layer already does — do not
  bypass it). Prefer CSS spring tokens (`.spring.snappy`, `.pop`) for
  state-driven motion; the JS spring engine (`animate`, `SpringValue`, the
  attachments) for gestures and layout.
- No new dependencies. No `any`. No `@ts-ignore`. No TODOs.
- Aesthetic bar: restrained, precise, premium. Hairline borders, the
  elevation ladder, generous but consistent spacing from the space ladder,
  `text-secondary`/`text-muted` for hierarchy, `.rim` + `.shad-*` on raised
  surfaces, `.glass` on floating ones, tabular numerals for numbers. Examples
  use realistic content (real product copy, never "foo"/"Lorem ipsum").

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` | the maxima extension layer — sources. `kits/<kit>.css` are the kit fragments |
| `src/lib/styles/custom.css` | GENERATED concat of the layers — fractalstyler's sanctioned `custom.css` extension point; the linter reads it |

Generated files carry a `GENERATED` banner — never edit them by hand.

## 4. House rules

- fractalstyler is consumed from `../fractalstyler` (linked). **Never edit
  anything in `../fractalstyler`.** Missing primitives go in the extension layer.
- Do not initialise git, commit, push or publish unless the user asks.

## 5. Motion and theme quick reference

Import inside `src/lib` from `'../../../motion/index.js'` / `'../../../theme/index.js'`;
in examples from `'@fractaldesign/maxima-ui/motion'` / `'/theme'` (also re-exported
from the root). Read the sources for the full JSDoc.

```ts
// springs — presets: 'gentle' | 'snappy' | 'bouncy' | 'stiff' | 'slow', or { stiffness, damping, mass }
springs, resolveSpring(input?), springDuration(input?), springEasing(input?), springEase(input?)

// engine — element must carry class "motion" (x y scale rotate opacity) or "tilt" (rotateX rotateY)
animate(node, { x, y, scale, rotate, opacity, rotateX, rotateY, '--custom': n }, { spring, instant, onUpdate }) → { finished, stop() }
setMotion(node, values)   getMotion(node, channel)
new SpringValue(initial, spring?)  → .current (reactive) .target .set(v, { instant })
reducedMotion.current

// attachments — {@attach name(options)}
vars({ value: 0.4 })                    // writes --value (any custom properties)
press() hover() magnetic() tilt()       // interaction springs
pointer()                               // writes --px/--py for spotlights
inView({ class: 'in' }) reveal() stagger()   // entrance; stagger writes --i on children
drag({ axis, bounds, snapBack, momentum, onDragEnd })
parallax() scrollProgress()
createFlip() → { attach, read(), play(), run(fn) }   // FLIP layout springs; items carry data-flip-id

// Svelte transitions with spring easing — transition:springScale={{ spring: 'bouncy' }}
springFade springFly springScale springBlur springSlide

// view transitions
startViewTransition(update, { type: 'fade'|'slide'|'slide-back'|'scale'|'reveal'|'none', origin })
setupViewTransitions(onNavigate, { type })    vtName('hero')   // element also needs class "vt-name"

// theme
theme (ThemeState: mode theme hue chroma tint radius density motion resolvedMode; setTheme() setMode() toggleMode(event) reset())
themes, initTheme(), themeInitScript()
```

CSS side (see `src/lib/styles/layers/10-motion.css`): `.spring` + `.spring-<preset>`
for state transitions, `.pop` + `.enter-*` for anything that opens (works on
`[popover]`, `<dialog open>`, and `.open`), `.anim-in` (staggered by `--i`),
`.reveal`/`.in`, `.lift`, `.press`.
# DESIGN

The design language of maxima-ui. It is fractalstyler's language, held to a
premium bar — restrained, precise, quiet until touched.

## Principles

1. **Composition over invention.** A component is a sentence written in
   fractalstyler's vocabulary. If two components look related, it is because
   they share classes, not because someone matched them by eye.
2. **Hierarchy through ink, not size.** `text-primary` → `text-secondary` →
   `text-muted` carry most hierarchy. Size and weight change rarely.
3. **Hairlines and light.** Surfaces are separated by 1px borders
   (`border`, `border-subtle`) and lifted by the elevation ladder (`shad-*`)
   with a lit top edge (`rim`). Floating surfaces are `glass`.
4. **Motion is physics.** Anything a person moves or triggers is driven by a
   spring — the same solver produces the CSS `linear()` tokens
   (`--spring-snappy` …) and drives the JavaScript engine, so a CSS transition
   and a dragged element settle the same way. Motion is interruptible, never
   blocks input, and collapses to nothing under reduced motion.
5. **One theme, three numbers.** `--hue`, `--chroma`, `--tint` generate every
   colour role in both modes. Shape (`data-radius`), density (`data-density`)
   and motion (`data-motion`) are independent axes that rewrite ladders, not
   components.

## The shared axes

| Axis | Values | Mechanism |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `variant` | primary · secondary · themed · soft · outline · ghost · link · info · success · warning · danger | a class of the same name |
| `size` | xs · sm · md · lg · xl | `sizeClass[size]` → height + text ladder |
| `shape` | rect · mincurved · modern · curved · round | a class of the same name |
| `tone` | neutral · info · success · warning · danger | status colour roles |

## The extension layer

| Layer | Adds |
|:---|:---|
| `00-tokens` | motion channels (`@property`), spring/motion scale, measure ladder |
| `01-springs` | generated `--spring-*` `linear()` easings |
| `10-motion` | `.motion` `.tilt` `.spring` `.pop` `.enter-*` `.anim-*` `.reveal`, view transitions |
| `20-surface` | `.glass` `.rim` `.glow` `.soft` `.measure-*` and small layout primitives |
| `30-overlay` | `.anchor` `.floating` `.dialog` `.sheet` `.layer` |
| `40-controls` | `.bare` `.item` `.track` `.fill` `.thumb` `.ring` `.indicator` `.caret` |
| `60-themes` | the parametric theme and the radius / density / motion axes |
| `kits/*` | ≤ 90 lines per kit, for primitives composition cannot express |

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {

		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;

		shape?: Shape;

		/** An icon drawn after the label. */

		size = 'md',
		shape = 'modern',

		{...rest as HTMLAnchorAttributes}

		{@render content()}
	</a>

		class={classes}
		{type}
		disabled={disabled || loading}
		aria-busy={loading || undefined}
		{@attach spring}
		{...rest}
	>
		{@render content()}

export { default as Button } from './Button.svelte';
import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',
	summary: 'Triggers an action or navigates, with a spring-loaded press.',
	description: `The button is the library's reference component: eleven variants, five sizes and five shapes, all of them plain fractalstyler classes, so a button always matches the inputs, tags and cards around it.

It renders a native \`<button>\` — or an \`<a>\` when you pass \`href\` — and forwards every attribute and event to it. Pressing it drives a real spring through the motion channel rather than a CSS keyframe, so a quick tap and a long hold both feel right.`,
	features: [
		'Eleven variants, five sizes, five shapes — shared with every other control',
		'Leading and trailing icons from @fractaldesign/icons',
		'Loading state that keeps the layout stable',
		'Renders a link when given href',
		'Interruptible spring press, disabled under reduced motion'
	],
	accessibility: [
		'Renders a native <button> (or <a> with href), so role, focus and activation come from the platform.',
		'While loading, the button is disabled and exposes aria-busy="true".',
		'An icon-only button needs an aria-label; icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.',
		'The focus ring is drawn only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible).'
	],
	keyboard: [
		{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' },
		{ keys: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the next focusable element.' }
	]
});
