// The gate's rules. Each check returns diagnostics; nothing here throws on bad input.

import ts from 'typescript';
import path from 'node:path';
import type { ComponentAnalysis, KitInfo } from './analysis.ts';
import { parseTs } from './api.ts';
import type { LayerBuild } from './css.ts';
import { extractScripts, markupOf, matchJsBrace, skipQuoted, stringLiterals } from './svelte.ts';
import { PATHS, closest, cssCodeLines, escapeRe, lineAt, listDir, readText, rel, walkFiles } from './util.ts';

export interface Diag {
	rule: string;
	severity: 'error' | 'warning';
	file: string;
	line: number | null;
	message: string;
	fix: string;
}

export const KIT_BUDGET = 90;

// ── the class allowlist ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface Allowlist {
	classes: Set<string>;
	stems: string[];
	registryFound: boolean;
}

export function loadAllowlist(layers: LayerBuild): Allowlist {
	const classes = new Set<string>();
	const stems: string[] = [];
	const raw = readText(PATHS.fsRegistry);
	let registryFound = false;
	if (raw) {
		try {
			const rows = JSON.parse(raw) as { class?: string }[];
			registryFound = Array.isArray(rows);
			for (const row of Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : []) {
				const name = (row.class ?? '').replace(/^\./, '').trim();
				if (!name) continue;
				if (name.includes('*')) stems.push(name.replace(/\*.*$/, ''));
				else classes.add(name);
			}
		} catch {
			registryFound = false;
		}
	}
	for (const c of layers.harvested) classes.add(c);
	return { classes, stems, registryFound };
}

export function isAllowed(cls: string, allow: Allowlist): boolean {
	return allow.classes.has(cls) || allow.stems.some((s) => cls.startsWith(s)) || /-(mob|desk)$/.test(cls);
}

function unknownClass(cls: string, file: string, line: number, allow: Allowlist): Diag {
	const near = closest(cls, allow.classes, 3);
	return {
		rule: 'class/unknown',
		severity: 'error',
		file,
		line,
		message: `class "${cls}" is not in the fractalstyler registry or the maxima extension layer`,
		fix: near.length
			? `did you mean ${near.map((n) => `"${n}"`).join(', ')}? (registry.md / src/lib/styles/layers)`
			: 'compose from registry.md, or add the smallest general primitive to your kit fragment'
	};
}

// ── class tokens in markup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

const CLASSY = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/;
const COMPARE_BEFORE = /(===|!==|==|!=|\bin|\bcase)\s*$/;
const COMPARE_AFTER = /^\s*(===|!==|==|!=|in\b)/;

/** Class-looking tokens of the string literals inside a JS expression (comparison operands skipped). */
function expressionClassTokens(expr: string): { token: string; offset: number }[] {
	const out: { token: string; offset: number }[] = [];
	for (const lit of stringLiterals(expr)) {
		if (lit.interpolated) continue;
		// comparison operands (`x === 'vertical'`), `case 'x':` labels and `'x' in o` are not class lists
		if (COMPARE_BEFORE.test(expr.slice(0, lit.start)) || COMPARE_AFTER.test(expr.slice(lit.end))) continue;
		let pos = 0;
		for (const tok of lit.value.split(/(\s+)/)) {
			if (tok && !/^\s+$/.test(tok) && CLASSY.test(tok)) out.push({ token: tok, offset: lit.start + 1 + pos });
			pos += tok.length;
		}
	}
	return out;
}

interface ScriptVar {
	init: string;
	offset: number;
}

/** `const x = …` / `let x = …` initialisers of the instance script, by name. */
function scriptVars(src: string): Map<string, ScriptVar> {
	const out = new Map<string, ScriptVar>();
	for (const s of extractScripts(src)) {
		const sf = parseTs(s.content, 'vars.ts');
		const visit = (n: ts.Node) => {
			if (ts.isVariableDeclaration(n) && ts.isIdentifier(n.name) && n.initializer) {
				const start = n.initializer.getStart(sf);
				out.set(n.name.text, { init: n.initializer.getText(sf), offset: s.offset + start });
			}
			ts.forEachChild(n, visit);
		};
		visit(sf);
	}
	return out;
}

export function checkSvelteClasses(file: string, src: string, allow: Allowlist): Diag[] {
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	const markup = markupOf(src);
	const vars = scriptVars(src);
	const relFile = rel(file);
	const checked = new Set<string>();
	const check = (cls: string, offset: number) => {
		if (!isAllowed(cls, allow)) out.push(unknownClass(cls, relFile, lineAt(src, offset), allow));
	};
	const checkExpr = (expr: string, base: number) => {
		for (const t of expressionClassTokens(expr)) check(t.token, base + t.offset);
		// identifiers that name script variables: check their initialisers too
		for (const m of expr.matchAll(/(?<![\w$.'"`-])([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)(?![\w$])/g)) {
			const v = vars.get(m[1]);
			if (!v || checked.has(m[1])) continue;
			checked.add(m[1]);
			for (const t of expressionClassTokens(v.init)) check(t.token, v.offset + t.offset);
		}
	};

	const ATTR = /(?<=[\s])class\s*=\s*/g;
	for (const m of markup.matchAll(ATTR)) {
		const at = (m.index ?? 0) + m[0].length;
		const q = markup[at];
		if (q === '"' || q === "'") {
			let i = at + 1;
			let staticText = '';
			while (i < markup.length && markup[i] !== q) {
				if (markup[i] === '{') {
					const close = matchJsBrace(markup, i);
					if (close < 0) break;
					checkExpr(markup.slice(i + 1, close), i + 1);
					staticText += ' '.repeat(close - i + 1);
					i = close + 1;
					continue;
				}
				staticText += markup[i];
				i++;
			}
			let pos = 0;
			for (const tok of staticText.split(/(\s+)/)) {
				if (tok && !/^\s+$/.test(tok)) check(tok, at + 1 + pos);
				pos += tok.length;
			}
		} else if (q === '{') {
			const close = matchJsBrace(markup, at);
			if (close > at) checkExpr(markup.slice(at + 1, close), at + 1);
		}
	}
	for (const m of markup.matchAll(/(?<=[\s])class:([\w-]+)/g)) check(m[1], m.index ?? 0);
	return out;
}

/** String literals of the exported `Record<…, string>` maps in tokens.ts. */
export function checkTokenMaps(allow: Allowlist): Diag[] {
	const src = readText(PATHS.tokensTs);
	if (!src) return [];
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	const sf = parseTs(src, 'tokens.ts');
	for (const st of sf.statements) {
		if (!ts.isVariableStatement(st) || !st.modifiers?.some((m) => m.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ExportKeyword)) continue;
		for (const d of st.declarationList.declarations) {
			if (!d.type || !/^Record</.test(d.type.getText(sf)) || !d.initializer || !ts.isObjectLiteralExpression(d.initializer)) continue;
			for (const p of d.initializer.properties) {
				if (!ts.isPropertyAssignment(p) || !ts.isStringLiteral(p.initializer)) continue;
				for (const tok of p.initializer.text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) {
					if (!isAllowed(tok, allow)) {
						out.push(unknownClass(tok, rel(PATHS.tokensTs), sf.getLineAndCharacterOfPosition(p.getStart(sf)).line + 1, allow));
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return out;
}

// ── Law 1: no styles, no svg, JS writes only custom properties ──────────────

function startsWithDashes(arg: ts.Expression | undefined): boolean {
	if (!arg) return false;
	if (ts.isStringLiteral(arg) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(arg)) return arg.text.startsWith('--');
	if (ts.isTemplateExpression(arg)) return arg.head.text.startsWith('--');
	return false;
}

function isStyleAccess(n: ts.Expression): boolean {
	return (ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(n) && n.name.text === 'style') || (ts.isElementAccessExpression(n) && ts.isStringLiteral(n.argumentExpression) && n.argumentExpression.text === 'style');
}

/** AST checks on one script / TS module. */
export function checkScriptAst(code: string, file: string, lineBase: number, inMotion: boolean): Diag[] {
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	const sf = parseTs(code, path.basename(file) + '.ts');
	const line = (n: ts.Node) => lineBase + sf.getLineAndCharacterOfPosition(n.getStart(sf)).line;
	const push = (n: ts.Node, message: string, fix: string) =>
		out.push({ rule: 'style/js-write', severity: 'error', file, line: line(n), message, fix });
	const CP_FIX = "write a custom property — node.style.setProperty('--x', v) or the vars() attachment — and let a class own the real property";

	const visit = (n: ts.Node) => {
		if (ts.isBinaryExpression(n) && n.operatorToken.kind >= ts.SyntaxKind.FirstAssignment && n.operatorToken.kind <= ts.SyntaxKind.LastAssignment) {
			const left = n.left;
			if (isStyleAccess(left)) push(n, 'assigns element.style directly', CP_FIX);
			else if ((ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(left) || ts.isElementAccessExpression(left)) && isStyleAccess(left.expression)) {
				const prop = ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(left) ? left.name.text : left.argumentExpression.getText(sf);
				push(n, prop === 'cssText' ? 'writes .style.cssText' : `assigns .style.${prop.replace(/['"]/g, '')}`, CP_FIX);
			}
		}
		if (ts.isCallExpression(n) && ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(n.expression)) {
			const method = n.expression.name.text;
			const target = n.expression.expression;
			if (method === 'setProperty' && isStyleAccess(target) && !startsWithDashes(n.arguments[0]) && !inMotion) {
				const lit = n.arguments[0] && (ts.isStringLiteral(n.arguments[0]) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(n.arguments[0]));
				push(
					n,
					lit ? `style.setProperty(${n.arguments[0].getText(sf)}) sets a real property` : 'style.setProperty() with a non-literal name (only src/lib/motion may)',
					"name a custom property literally: setProperty('--x', …)"
				);
			}
			if (method === 'setAttribute' && n.arguments[0] && (ts.isStringLiteral(n.arguments[0]) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(n.arguments[0])) && n.arguments[0].text.toLowerCase() === 'style') {
				push(n, "setAttribute('style', …)", CP_FIX);
			}
			if (method === 'assign' && target.getText(sf) === 'Object' && n.arguments[0] && isStyleAccess(n.arguments[0])) {
				push(n, 'Object.assign(element.style, …)', CP_FIX);
			}
		}
		ts.forEachChild(n, visit);
	};
	visit(sf);
	return out;
}

// ── imports ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const LIB_BARE = /^(svelte(\/.*)?|@fractaldesign\/icons(\/.*)?)$/;
const EXAMPLE_ALLOWED = /^(svelte(\/.*)?|@fractaldesign\/icons(\/.*)?|@fractaldesign\/maxima-ui(\/motion|\/theme)?)$/;

export function moduleSpecifiers(code: string): { spec: string; line: number }[] {
	const sf = parseTs(code, 'imports.ts');
	const out: { spec: string; line: number }[] = [];
	const add = (lit: ts.Expression | undefined) => {
		if (lit && ts.isStringLiteral(lit)) out.push({ spec: lit.text, line: sf.getLineAndCharacterOfPosition(lit.getStart(sf)).line });
	};
	const visit = (n: ts.Node) => {
		if (ts.isImportDeclaration(n) || ts.isExportDeclaration(n)) add(n.moduleSpecifier);
		else if (ts.isCallExpression(n) && n.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ImportKeyword) add(n.arguments[0]);
		else if (ts.isImportTypeNode(n) && ts.isLiteralTypeNode(n.argument)) add(n.argument.literal);
		ts.forEachChild(n, visit);
	};
	visit(sf);
	return out;
}

export function checkImports(code: string, file: string, lineBase: number, isExample: boolean): Diag[] {
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	for (const { spec, line } of moduleSpecifiers(code)) {
		let bad = false;
		let fix = '';
		if (isExample) {
			if (!EXAMPLE_ALLOWED.test(spec)) {
				bad = true;
				fix = "examples import exactly what a consumer writes: '@fractaldesign/maxima-ui' (/motion, /theme), '@fractaldesign/icons*', 'svelte*'";
			}
		} else if (spec.startsWith('.')) {
			const target = path.resolve(path.dirname(path.join(PATHS.root, file)), spec);
			if (!target.startsWith(PATHS.lib + path.sep)) {
				bad = true;
				fix = 'relative imports must stay inside src/lib';
			}
		} else if (!LIB_BARE.test(spec)) {
			bad = true;
			fix = "inside src/lib import relatively (no $lib, no #lib); only 'svelte*' and '@fractaldesign/icons*' are bare";
		}
		if (bad) out.push({ rule: 'import/forbidden', severity: 'error', file, line: lineBase + line, message: `import '${spec}'`, fix });
	}
	return out;
}

// ── per-file Law 1 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const GLYPHS = /[✓✔✗✘✕✖☰▾▴▸◂▶◀★☆⨯]/;

export function checkFile(full: string, allow: Allowlist | null): Diag[] {
	const file = rel(full);
	const src = readText(full);
	if (src === null) return [];
	const out: Diag[] = [];
	const inMotion = full.startsWith(PATHS.motion + path.sep);
	const isExample = file.split('/').includes('examples');
	try {
		if (full.endsWith('.svelte')) {
			const noComments = src.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' '));
			const markup = markupOf(src);
			const styleBlock = noComments.search(/<style[\s>]/);
			if (styleBlock >= 0)
				out.push({ rule: 'style/block', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, styleBlock), message: '<style> block', fix: 'delete it; compose fractalstyler classes in markup' });
			for (const m of markup.matchAll(/\sstyle\s*=/g))
				out.push({ rule: 'style/inline', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, m.index ?? 0), message: 'style="…" attribute', fix: 'use classes; pass dynamic values as custom properties with the vars() attachment' });
			for (const m of markup.matchAll(/\sstyle:([\w-]+)/g))
				out.push({ rule: 'style/inline', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, m.index ?? 0), message: `style:${m[1]} directive`, fix: 'use classes; pass dynamic values as custom properties with the vars() attachment' });
			for (const m of noComments.matchAll(/<svg[\s>/]/g))
				out.push({ rule: 'icons/inline-svg', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, m.index ?? 0), message: 'inline <svg>', fix: "use <Icon icon={luName} /> from '@fractaldesign/icons'" });
			// visible text only: strip tags and expressions
			const text = markup.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ')).replace(/\{[^}]*\}/g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' '));
			const g = text.search(GLYPHS);
			if (g >= 0)
				out.push({ rule: 'icons/glyph', severity: 'warning', file, line: lineAt(src, g), message: `unicode glyph "${text[g]}" used as an icon`, fix: "use <Icon icon={luName} /> from '@fractaldesign/icons'" });
			for (const m of markup.matchAll(/\.style\.(cssText|[a-zA-Z]+)\s*=(?!=)|setAttribute\(\s*['"`]style['"`]/g))
				out.push({ rule: 'style/js-write', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, m.index ?? 0), message: `writes a real style property in markup (${m[0].trim()})`, fix: "write a custom property — setProperty('--x', v) or vars()" });
			for (const s of extractScripts(src)) {
				out.push(...checkScriptAst(s.content, file, s.line, inMotion));
				out.push(...checkImports(s.content, file, s.line, isExample));
			}
			if (allow) out.push(...checkSvelteClasses(full, src, allow));
		} else if (full.endsWith('.ts')) {
			out.push(...checkScriptAst(src, file, 1, inMotion));
			out.push(...checkImports(src, file, 1, isExample));
			const noComments = src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|\/\/[^\n]*/g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' '));
			for (const m of noComments.matchAll(/<svg[\s>/]/g))
				out.push({ rule: 'icons/inline-svg', severity: 'error', file, line: lineAt(src, m.index ?? 0), message: 'inline <svg> markup in a string', fix: "use <Icon icon={luName} /> from '@fractaldesign/icons'" });
		}
	} catch (err) {
		out.push({ rule: 'analysis/crash', severity: 'error', file, line: null, message: `could not analyse: ${(err as Error).message}`, fix: 'fix the syntax error' });
	}
	return out;
}

export function readLayers(): LayerFile[] {

const BANNER =

export function buildLayers(files: LayerFile[] = readLayers()): LayerBuild {
	const parts: string[] = [BANNER, ''];
	const segments: LayerSegment[] = [];
	let line = 3;
	for (const f of files) {

		parts.push(`/* ── ${f.name} ── */`);

		const n = body === '' ? 0 : body.split('\n').length;
		segments.push({ file: f.name, start: line, lines: n });
		if (n > 0) parts.push(body);
		parts.push('');
		line += n + 1;

export function mapCustomLine(segments: LayerSegment[], line: number): { file: string; line: number } | null {
	for (const s of segments) {

	}

/** Every component folder, kits in kits.ts order (unknown kits after, sorted), names sorted. */
export function listComponents(kits: KitInfo[] = readKits()): ComponentRef[] {
	const order = new Map(kits.map((k, i) => [k.id, i]));
	const kitDirs = listDir(PATHS.components, 'dir').sort((a, b) => {
		const ia = order.get(a) ?? 1e6;
		const ib = order.get(b) ?? 1e6;
		return ia - ib || byCodepoint(a, b);
	});
	const out: ComponentRef[] = [];
	for (const kit of kitDirs) {
		for (const slug of listDir(path.join(PATHS.components, kit), 'dir')) {
			const dir = path.join(PATHS.components, kit, slug);
			out.push({ kit, slug, dir, relDir: rel(dir) });
		}
	}

}

## 1. The two laws

### Law 1 — fractalstyler only

Styling is **composition of registered classes in markup**. Nothing else.

- NO `<style>` blocks. NO `style="…"`. NO `style:prop` directives.
- NO raw hex colours, NO pixel literals above 2px, NO literal `border-radius`.
- NO inline `<svg>` and NO unicode glyph icons — icons are
  `import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons'` +
  `import { luCheck } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide'` → `<Icon icon={luCheck} />`.
  (Check a name exists: `grep -c "luName\b" node_modules/@fractaldesign/icons/dist/lucide.d.ts`.)
- Every class must exist in **fractalstyler's registry**
  (`node_modules/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/registry.md` — read it) or in the
  **maxima extension layer** (`src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` — read them; they
  are short).
- Modifiers are never standalone: `.row.xcenter`, never a bare `.xcenter`.
- There is no `.w-*`, `.pad-x-*`, `.border-top`. Search the registry; never guess.

**Dynamic values travel through custom properties.** JavaScript may write
*only* custom properties — `node.style.setProperty('--x', …)` — and a class
owns the real property (`translate: calc(var(--mx, 0) * 1px) …`). Use the
`vars()` attachment (`src/lib/motion`) to bind values:
`<div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: 0.4 })}>`. Never assign
`node.style.transform = …` or any real property.

**The extension layer is small on purpose.** Compose first. If the system
genuinely cannot express something, add the *smallest general primitive* to
your kit's fragment `src/lib/styles/layers/kits/<kit>.css`:

- plain CSS, tokens only (`var(--space-*)`, `var(--radius-*)`, colour roles),
  `rem`/`em`/`%` — no px above 2, no hex, no `&` nesting;
- named in the system's voice (`.track`, `.thumb`, `.indicator`) — a
  primitive several components could use, not `.my-component-inner`;
- hard budget: **90 lines per kit fragment**. The gate fails above it;
- only edit your own kit's fragment. Never edit `custom.css` (generated) or
  another layer file. After editing run `pnpm gen`.

### Law 2 — a component and its documentation are one

A component is a **folder**. It is not done until the folder passes
`pnpm verify <kit>/<name>`:

```
src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/        # <name> is kebab-case
  <Name>.svelte                         # the primary component (PascalCase of <name>)
  <NamePart>.svelte …                   # optional further parts (DialogTitle.svelte)
  <name>.svelte.ts | <name>.ts          # optional logic/state modules
  index.ts                              # named exports of every public thing
  doc.ts                                # the documentation manifest
  examples/01-usage.svelte              # ≥ 1, ordered by numeric prefix
  examples/02-….svelte
```

The docs page is **generated** from that folder — you never write a route:

- **Install / import** — generated from the package name and `index.ts`.
- **Examples** — each example file is rendered live *and* shown as source
  (the same file, so demo and code cannot drift).
- **API tables** — extracted from each part's `interface Props` and its JSDoc.
- **Accessibility / keyboard** — from `doc.ts`.

What the gate requires:

1. `index.ts` exports the primary component and every part
   (`export { default as Button } from './Button.svelte';`).
2. Every exported `.svelte` part declares `interface Props` in its instance
   script. **Every prop has a JSDoc comment** (one sentence or more). Defaults
   are documented by the destructuring default or an explicit `@default` tag.
3. `doc.ts` default-exports `defineDoc({...})` (shape below), nothing empty.
4. Each example starts with the header line
   `<!-- @example Title :: One sentence describing what it shows. -->`
   and example 01 is the minimal usage.
5. **Coverage — nothing is left out.** Across the folder's examples:
   every value of every string-literal-union prop (`variant`, `size`, `shape`,
   `placement`, …) appears; every prop name declared in `Props` (of every part)
   appears. (`class`, `children`, `ref` are exempt.)
6. Law 1, statically: no style blocks/attributes/directives, no `<svg`, no
   `.style.` writes other than `setProperty('--…')`, and every class token in a
   `class="…"` / `class={…}` literal is registered.
7. Inside `src/lib`, imports are **relative** (no `#lib`, no `$lib`). Examples
   import only from `@fractaldesign/maxima-ui` (and `/motion`, `/theme`),
   `@fractaldesign/icons*`, and `svelte*` — exactly what a consumer would write.

### `doc.ts`

```ts
import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',                       // the primary export
	summary: 'One sentence. Shown in the index and the page header.',
	description: `One to three paragraphs. Blank line = new paragraph. \`code\` allowed.`,
	parts: { ButtonGroup: 'One line: what this part is for.' },   // optional, every non-primary .svelte export
	features: ['Spring-pressed', '…'],    // optional bullets
	accessibility: ['Renders a native <button> …'],               // ≥ 1
	keyboard: [{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' }],   // when interactive
	api: [{ name: 'toast(message, options?)', type: '(…) => string', description: '…' }], // non-component exports
	related: ['icon-button']              // optional slugs
});
```

## 2. Authoring conventions

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { sizeClass, type Size, type Shape, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style of the button. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The content. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let { variant = 'primary', size = 'md', class: klass, children, ...rest }: Props = $props();
</script>

<button class={['button', variant, sizeClass[size], klass]} {...rest}>
	{@render children?.()}
</button>
```

- Runes only: `$props`, `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$bindable`,
  `$props.id()` for ids. Snippets, never slots. `{@attach}`, never `use:`.
  Callback props (`onchange`), never `createEventDispatcher`.
- `class` is always accepted and merged last via the array form
  `class={['…', cond && '…', klass]}`. Spread `...rest` onto the root element
  and extend the matching `svelte/elements` attribute type.
- Two-way state is `$bindable()` **and** has a callback
  (`value = $bindable()`, `onValueChange`). Works controlled and uncontrolled.
- Shared axes come from `src/lib/internal/tokens.ts` — do not redefine:
  `Variant` (`primary secondary themed outline ghost link soft info success
  warning danger`), `Size` (`xs sm md lg xl` → `sizeClass[size]`), `Shape`
  (`rect mincurved modern curved round`), `Tone` (`neutral info success
  warning danger`), `Placement`.
- Compound components share state with `createContext` from `svelte`
  (`const [getTabs, setTabs] = createContext<TabsState>()`).
- Use the platform first: native `<dialog>`, the Popover API (`popover`
  attribute), CSS anchor positioning (`.anchor` / `.floating`, see
  `src/lib/internal/floating.ts`), `<details>`, `:has()`, `@starting-style`
  enter/exit (`.pop` + `.enter-*`). JavaScript only where the platform stops.
- SSR-safe: no `window`/`document` at module or init time — only inside
  `$effect`, attachments and event handlers.
- Accessible by construction: correct roles, `aria-*` wiring, labels, focus
  management, full keyboard support (document it in `doc.ts`).
- Motion (all from `src/lib/motion`): springs for anything a user moves or
  triggers; honour reduced motion (the motion layer already does — do not
  bypass it). Prefer CSS spring tokens (`.spring.snappy`, `.pop`) for
  state-driven motion; the JS spring engine (`animate`, `SpringValue`, the
  attachments) for gestures and layout.
- No new dependencies. No `any`. No `@ts-ignore`. No TODOs.
- Aesthetic bar: restrained, precise, premium. Hairline borders, the
  elevation ladder, generous but consistent spacing from the space ladder,
  `text-secondary`/`text-muted` for hierarchy, `.rim` + `.shad-*` on raised
  surfaces, `.glass` on floating ones, tabular numerals for numbers. Examples
  use realistic content (real product copy, never "foo"/"Lorem ipsum").

## 3. Map

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` | the maxima extension layer — sources. `kits/<kit>.css` are the kit fragments |
| `src/lib/styles/custom.css` | GENERATED concat of the layers — fractalstyler's sanctioned `custom.css` extension point; the linter reads it |
| `src/lib/internal/` | shared tokens, floating/anchor helpers, list navigation, highlight |
| `src/lib/motion/` | spring solver, CSS spring tokens, `animate`, attachments, transitions, view transitions |
| `src/lib/theme/` | parametric theme runtime (mode, theme, hue/chroma, radius, density, motion) |
| `src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/` | the components — see Law 2 |
| `src/lib/components/kits.ts` | the kit list (order, titles) |
| `src/lib/docs/` | `defineDoc`, doc types, GENERATED `api.json` |
| `src/lib/index.ts` | GENERATED barrel |
| `src/routes/` | the docs site — generated pages + hand-written guides |
| `scripts/` | `gen.ts`, `gate.ts`, `verify.ts` and friends |

Generated files carry a `GENERATED` banner — never edit them by hand.

## 4. House rules

- fractalstyler is consumed from `../fractalstyler` (linked). **Never edit
  anything in `../fractalstyler`.** Missing primitives go in the extension layer.
- Do not initialise git, commit, push or publish unless the user asks.
- Work only in the paths you were assigned; other agents are working in
  parallel in sibling folders. Never "fix" a sibling's files — report instead.

/** The documentation manifest of one component folder. See AGENTS.md, Law 2. */
export interface ComponentDoc {
	/** The primary export, PascalCase — `Button`. */
	name: string;
	/** One sentence. Shown in the index and the page header. */
	summary: string;
	/** One to three paragraphs. A blank line starts a new paragraph; `code` is allowed. */
	description: string;
	/** Every non-primary component export → one line on what it is for. */
	parts?: Record<string, string>;
	/** Short capability bullets. */
	features?: string[];
	/** How the component is accessible — at least one statement. */
	accessibility: string[];
	/** Keyboard interactions, when the component is interactive. */
	keyboard?: { keys: string; action: string }[];
	/** Non-component exports: functions, attachments, classes, stores. */
	api?: { name: string; type: string; description: string }[];
	/** Slugs of related components. */
	related?: string[];
	status?: 'stable' | 'beta';
}

export function defineDoc(doc: ComponentDoc): ComponentDoc {
	return doc;
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// fractalstyler lint — the design system contract linter & agent guard.
//
// Verifies code against the styling system contract:
//   - Svelte files: no scoped <style>, no style="..." attributes, all classes verified
//   - Stylesheets: token purity (no raw hex, >2px budget, valid var(--tokens))
//   - Sass files: valid interpolation, radius ladder usage
//
// Supports:
//   Self mode:     node lint/cli.ts               (inside fractalstyler repo)
//   Consumer mode: node lint/cli.ts <dir>         (linting any project using fractalstyler)
//   Flags:         --json (agent/CI output), --own <file>, --registry <file>
//
// Source is TypeScript, run directly on Node 24 in the repo; the published
// package ships the lint/cli.mjs that `pnpm build:runtime` emits next to it.
// =============================================================================

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { loadRegistry } from './lib/registry.ts';
import { lintSvelteFile } from './lib/svelte-linter.ts';
import { TokenLinter } from './lib/token-linter.ts';
import { lintHardcodedRadius, lintSassNesting } from './lib/css-linter.ts';
import { reportDiagnostics, type Diagnostic } from './lib/agent-reporter.ts';

const PKG_ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');

function usage() {
	console.log(`Usage:
  fractalstyler lint              # self mode: audit fractalstyler package
  fractalstyler lint <dir>        # consumer mode: audit project directory
Options:
  --own <file>    extension stylesheet (default <dir>/src/lib/styles/custom.css)
  --registry <f>  registry.json override
  --json          machine-readable JSON diagnostics for agents and CI
  --help          show this help message`);
}

interface Flags {
	json: boolean;
	own: string | null;
	registry: string | null;
}

const SVELTE = /\.svelte$/;
const STYLESHEET = /\.(sass|scss|css)$/;

function walk(
	dir: string,
	filter: (name: string) => boolean,
	out: string[] = [],
	base = dir,
	skip: (relativePath: string) => boolean = () => false,
	root = dir
): string[] {
	if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return out;
	for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
		if (
			entry.name === 'node_modules' ||
			entry.name === '.svelte-kit' ||
			entry.name === 'dist' ||
			entry.name === '.git' ||
			entry.name === 'reserve' ||
			entry.name.startsWith('.')
		)
			continue;

		const full = path.join(base, entry.name);
		if (skip(path.relative(root, full))) continue;
		if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(full, filter, out, full, skip, root);
		else if (filter(entry.name)) out.push(full);
	}
	return out;
}

const rel = (root: string, file: string) => path.relative(root, file);

function harvestOwnClasses(content: string): Set<string> {
	const names = new Set<string>();
	for (const m of content.matchAll(/(?:^|[\s,{}])(\.)([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)/g)) {
		names.add(m[2]);
	}
	return names;
}

function collectLocalProperties(stylesheets: string[]): Set<string> {
	const names = new Set<string>();
	for (const file of stylesheets) {
		try {
			const content = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
			for (const m of content.matchAll(/(--[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\s*:/g)) {
				names.add(m[1]);
			}
		} catch {}
	}
	return names;
}

async function lintSelf(flags: Flags): Promise<Diagnostic[]> {
	const diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
	const { classes, tokens, stems } = loadRegistry(PKG_ROOT, flags.registry);
	const tokenLinter = new TokenLinter(PKG_ROOT, { tokens });

	// 1. Lint Svelte files in src/
	//    src/lib/components is the in-progress sveltemodular workspace — it is
	//    not part of the styling system yet, so it is not held to the contract.
	const svelteFiles = walk(path.join(PKG_ROOT, 'src'), (f) => SVELTE.test(f), [], path.join(PKG_ROOT, 'src'), (relative) =>
		relative.split(path.sep).slice(0, 2).join('/') === 'lib/components'
	);
	for (const file of svelteFiles) {
		const source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
		const relPath = rel(PKG_ROOT, file);
		const result = lintSvelteFile(relPath, source, { allowlist: classes, stems });
		diagnostics.push(...result.diagnostics);
	}

	// 2. Lint the stylesheets in src/lib/styles
	const styleFiles = walk(path.join(PKG_ROOT, 'src', 'lib', 'styles'), (f) => STYLESHEET.test(f));
	for (const file of styleFiles) {
		const source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
		const relPath = rel(PKG_ROOT, file);
		diagnostics.push(...lintSassNesting(relPath, source));
	}

	return diagnostics;
}

async function lintConsumer(targetDir: string, flags: Flags): Promise<Diagnostic[]> {
	const diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
	const targetRoot = path.resolve(targetDir);

	// Load canonical registry from fractalstyler package
	const { classes: canonicalClasses, tokens, stems } = loadRegistry(PKG_ROOT, flags.registry);

	// Find consumer's own extension classes
	const ownFile = flags.own
		? path.resolve(flags.own)
		: path.join(targetRoot, 'src', 'lib', 'styles', 'custom.css');

	const ownClasses = new Set<string>();
	if (fs.existsSync(ownFile)) {
		const ownContent = fs.readFileSync(ownFile, 'utf8');
		for (const cls of harvestOwnClasses(ownContent)) {
			ownClasses.add(cls);
		}
	}

	// Full allowlist = canonical registry union with own classes
	const allowlist = new Set([...canonicalClasses, ...ownClasses]);

	// Collect locally defined CSS variables across target
	const stylesheets = walk(targetRoot, (f) => STYLESHEET.test(f));
	const localProps = collectLocalProperties(stylesheets);

	const tokenLinter = new TokenLinter(targetRoot, { tokens });

	// Lint Svelte files
	const svelteFiles = walk(targetRoot, (f) => SVELTE.test(f));
	for (const file of svelteFiles) {
		const source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
		const relPath = rel(targetRoot, file);
		const result = lintSvelteFile(relPath, source, { allowlist, stems });
		diagnostics.push(...result.diagnostics);
	}

	// Lint stylesheets (the system layers are the package's own; a consumer's
	// own stylesheet is theirs to lint)
	for (const file of stylesheets) {
		const base = path.basename(file);
		// The system layers belong to the package: they are where the hex and
		// the ladders live. A consumer's own stylesheet is not exempt.
		if (base === 'index.css') continue;

		const source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
		const relPath = rel(targetRoot, file);

		diagnostics.push(...tokenLinter.lintFile(relPath, source, localProps));
		diagnostics.push(...lintSassNesting(relPath, source));
		diagnostics.push(...lintHardcodedRadius(relPath, source));
	}

	return diagnostics;
}

async function main() {
	const args = process.argv.slice(2);
	const flags: Flags = { json: false, own: null, registry: null };
	const positional: string[] = [];

	for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
		const arg = args[i];
		if (arg === '--help' || arg === '-h') {
			usage();
			process.exit(0);
		} else if (arg === '--json') {
			flags.json = true;
		} else if (arg === '--own' && i + 1 < args.length) {
			flags.own = args[++i];
		} else if (arg === '--registry' && i + 1 < args.length) {
			flags.registry = args[++i];
		} else if (!arg.startsWith('-')) {
			positional.push(arg);
		}
	}

	const targetDir = positional[0] === 'lint' ? positional[1] : positional[0];

	let diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
	try {
		if (!targetDir || targetDir === '.') {
			diagnostics = await lintSelf(flags);
		} else {
			diagnostics = await lintConsumer(targetDir, flags);
		}

		reportDiagnostics(diagnostics, { json: flags.json });
		const hasErrors = diagnostics.some((d) => d.severity === 'error');
		process.exit(hasErrors ? 1 : 0);
	} catch (err) {
		console.error(`\x1b[31mError during lint: ${(err as Error).message}\x1b[0m`);
		if (process.env.DEBUG) console.error(err);
		process.exit(2);
	}
}

main();
// =============================================================================
// Registry loader — the source of truth for every class and token check.
//
// Reads registry.json and pairs it with compiled stylesheet verification
// so loop-generated wildcard families (.gap-*, .pad-*, .radius-*) and exact
// selectors are both known without guesswork.
// =============================================================================

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

/** A registry.json row in the flat array format (what scripts/update-registry emits). */
interface RegistryRow {
	class?: string;
	layer?: string;
	file?: string;
}

/** The layered registry format: { layers: [{ id, file, items }] }. */
interface RegistryLayer {
	id: string;
	file?: string;
	items?: { kind: string; name: string }[];
}

export interface LoadedRegistry {
	classes: Set<string>;
	tokens: Set<string>;
	ownLayerClasses: Set<string>;
	layerIds: Set<string>;
	layerOf: Map<string, string>;
	fileOfLayer: Map<string, string>;
	stems: string[];
}

/**
 * Loads the style registry for verification.
 * @param rootDir Root of the fractalstyler package or consumer project.
 * @param registryPath Path to registry.json override.
 */
export function loadRegistry(rootDir: string, registryPath?: string | null): LoadedRegistry {
	const defaultRegistry = path.join(rootDir, 'registry.json');
	const regFile = registryPath || (fs.existsSync(defaultRegistry) ? defaultRegistry : path.join(rootDir, 'src', 'lib', 'data', 'registry.json'));

	if (!fs.existsSync(regFile)) {
		throw new Error(`registry.json not found at ${regFile} — run "pnpm registry" first.`);
	}

	const data: RegistryRow[] | { layers?: RegistryLayer[] } = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(regFile, 'utf8'));
	const classes = new Set<string>();
	const tokens = new Set<string>();
	const ownLayerClasses = new Set<string>();
	const layerIds = new Set<string>();
	const layerOf = new Map<string, string>();
	const fileOfLayer = new Map<string, string>();
	const stems: string[] = [];

	// 1. Process registry.json (handles both array format and { layers: [...] } format)
	if (Array.isArray(data)) {
		for (const entry of data) {
			const rawClass = (entry.class || '').replace(/^\./, '').trim();
			if (!rawClass) continue;

			if (rawClass.includes('*')) {
				stems.push(rawClass.replace(/\*.*$/, ''));
			} else {
				classes.add(rawClass);
			}

			const layer = entry.layer || 'L0';
			layerIds.add(layer);
			layerOf.set(rawClass, layer);
			if (entry.file) fileOfLayer.set(layer, entry.file);

			if (layer.toLowerCase().includes('own') || (entry.file && entry.file.includes('own'))) {
				ownLayerClasses.add(rawClass);
			}
		}
	} else if (data.layers && Array.isArray(data.layers)) {
		for (const layer of data.layers) {
			const isOwn = /own/i.test(layer.id || '') || /own/i.test(layer.file || '');
			layerIds.add(layer.id);
			if (!fileOfLayer.has(layer.id)) fileOfLayer.set(layer.id, layer.file || layer.id);

			for (const item of layer.items || []) {
				if (item.kind === 'class') {
					const name = item.name.replace(/^\./, '');
					if (name.includes('*')) {
						stems.push(name.replace(/\*.*$/, ''));
					} else {
						classes.add(name);
					}
					if (!layerOf.has(name)) layerOf.set(name, layer.id);
					if (isOwn) ownLayerClasses.add(name);
				} else if (item.kind === 'token') {
					tokens.add(item.name);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// 2. Also harvest the stylesheets themselves — the registry records what a
	//    class means, the stylesheet is what decides whether it exists.
	const stylesDir = path.join(rootDir, 'src', 'lib', 'styles');
	if (fs.existsSync(stylesDir)) {
		for (const file of fs.readdirSync(stylesDir).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.css'))) {
			const content = fs.readFileSync(path.join(stylesDir, file), 'utf8');
			for (const match of content.matchAll(/\.([a-zA-Z][\w-]*)/g)) classes.add(match[1]);
			for (const match of content.matchAll(/(--[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\s*:/g)) tokens.add(match[1]);
		}
	}

	return { classes, tokens, ownLayerClasses, layerIds, layerOf, fileOfLayer, stems };
}
// =============================================================================
// Svelte contract scanner for fractalstyler.
//
// Zero-dependency regex scanner that runs via CLI or in CI. Enforces:
//   fs/no-in-component-styles — no scoped <style> blocks.
//   fs/no-inline-styles       — no style="..." attributes.
//   fs/unknown-class          — every class used in markup must exist in registry.
// =============================================================================

import type { Diagnostic } from './agent-reporter.ts';
import { findClosestMatches } from './fuzzy.ts';

const CLASS_ATTR = /\sclass\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')/g;
const CLASS_DIRECTIVE = /\sclass:([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)/g;
const STYLE_BLOCK = /<style[\s>]/;
const STYLE_ATTR = /\sstyle\s*=/;

export interface SvelteLintOptions {
	allowlist?: Set<string>;
	stems?: string[];
}

/** Lints a Svelte file for styling system compliance. */
export function lintSvelteFile(
	relPath: string,
	source: string,
	options: SvelteLintOptions = {}
): { diagnostics: Diagnostic[]; classes: Set<string> } {
	const diagnostics: Diagnostic[] = [];
	const classes = new Set<string>();
	const { allowlist, stems = [] } = options;

	// Rule 1: No scoped <style> blocks
	if (STYLE_BLOCK.test(source)) {
		const line = source.slice(0, source.search(STYLE_BLOCK)).split('\n').length;
		diagnostics.push({
			rule: 'fs/no-in-component-styles',
			severity: 'error',
			file: relPath,
			line,
			found: '<style> block detected',
			rationale:
				'Components must remain pure markup & logic. Scoped styles fragment the design system, block global theme changes, and leak ad-hoc CSS.',
			suggestion:
				'Remove the <style> block and express the design using fractalstyler classes. If a class is missing, add it to the designated stylesheet in src/lib/styles or your custom.css.'
		});
	}

	// Strip <script> content first so JS assignments like `style = ...` are not flagged
	const scriptStart = source.indexOf('<script');
	let markup = source;
	if (scriptStart !== -1) {

---
title: Layout Shell
description: Explains the app shell classes - header, main, sidebars, footer and content widths - in layout-shell.css.
id: 7
---

This document explains `layout-shell.css`, the app/site chrome skeleton. It composes with the tokens from [Configurations](./01-configurations.md): `--header-height`, `--footer-height`, `--fit-height`, `--app-inline`, `--content-clamp`, `--sidebar-width-left/right`, and the z-index scale.

There are Svelte components that render exactly this markup — see [Layout](./16-layout.md).

## Structure

```html
<div class="app-shell">
  <header class="app-header">…</header>
  <div class="app-main">
    <aside class="sidebar-left">…</aside>
    <div class="main-section">…</div>
    <aside class="sidebar-right">…</aside>
  </div>
  <footer class="app-footer">…</footer>
</div>
```

- `.app-shell` - column flex, min-height 100vh
- `.app-header` - sticky at top, `--z-sticky`, fixed `--header-height`, `--app-inline` padding; `.clamped` caps it to `--content-clamp`
- `.app-main` - the flex-grow row holding sidebars + content; each sidebar is sticky below the header for the remaining viewport height
- `.main-section` - the flex-grow content column; `.solo` (no sidebars) applies `--app-inline` padding
- `.app-footer` - row flex, `--app-inline` padding, min `--footer-height`

## Sidebar responsiveness

- below 1025px both sidebars are hidden; `.app-shell.open .sidebar-left` shows the left sidebar as a fixed overlay at `--z-modal` (mobile drawer)
- at 1025px+ the left sidebar shows, sticky
- at 1281px+ the right sidebar shows too

Lists inside sidebars get their left margin/padding zeroed.

## Content widths

`.content-section` wraps page content and is a column flex container. `.narrow-full`, `.narrow-half` and `.narrow-wide` are centered reading-width presets that grow with breakpoints:

| Breakpoint | narrow-full | narrow-half | narrow-wide |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 769px+ | - | 640px | 720px |
| 1025px+ | 640px | 750px | 750px |
| 1281px+ | 720px | 800px | 1024px |
| 1441px+ | - | 1024px | 1280px |

`narrow-half` gets increasing right padding at larger sizes to leave room for a right sidebar. `.content-section.null` and `.solo`-less main sections handle the un-padded edge cases.

`.page-header` is a column flex container for a page's title block (see [Typography](./05-typography.md) for `.page-title` and `.page-desc`).

The left sidebar draws a thin scrollbar: 2px wide, transparent track and a pill thumb in WebKit, and a light thumb on `--bg` through `scrollbar-color` elsewhere.

For the vertical fitment alternative (a central area filling the viewport minus header/footer), see the `hfull-fitted` class in [Shapes and Sizes](./03-shapes-sizes.md).
---
title: Layout
description: The Svelte components that render the application shell — header, main, sidebars, footer — and the layout state that fills them.
id: 16
---

`src/lib/layout/` is the Svelte 5 layer over `layout-shell.css`. The
stylesheet defines *what* the shell looks like; these components define the
**canonical markup** — so nobody has to remember that the header is
`.app-header`, that the content column is `.main-section`, or that the left
rail is `.sidebar-left`.

Every component is a thin wrapper: it renders one canonical class, takes a
`class` for your own additions, and accepts `children` as a snippet. None of
them writes a style.

## The anatomy

```
.app-shell                    ← AppShell
├── .app-header              ← header slot
├── .app-main                 ← the row
│   ├── .sidebar-left         ← left slot (a drawer below 1025px)
│   ├── .main-section        ← the children
│   └── .sidebar-right        ← right slot (from 1281px)
└── .app-footer              ← footer slot
```

## The components

### `AppShell` — the whole chrome

The one component that renders the shell. Every region is optional, and every
region can be filled by a prop **or** by the shared layout state.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `header` | `Snippet` | — | the header content |
| `sidebarLeft` | `Snippet` | — | the left rail |
| `sidebarRight` | `Snippet` | — | the right rail |
| `footer` | `Snippet` | — | the footer content |
| `children` | `Snippet` | — | the main column |
| `clamped` | `boolean` | `false` | limits the header and main to the content width (`--content-clamp`), centred |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | opens the left drawer — the shell gets `.open` |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | added to the shell |

```svelte
<script>
	import { AppShell } from '$lib/layout';
</script>

<AppShell clamped>
	{#snippet header()}
		<strong>My app</strong>
	{/snippet}

	{#snippet sidebarLeft()}
		<nav class="box gap-sm">
			<a class="nav-link" href="/">Home</a>
		</nav>
	{/snippet}

	<h1>Hello</h1>
</AppShell>
```

### `AppHeader` / `AppFooter`

The two ends of the shell, for when you compose the regions yourself instead
of using the shell.

```svelte
<AppHeader clamped>
	<strong>My app</strong>
</AppHeader>
```

| Component | Prop | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `AppHeader` | `clamped` | limits the header to the content width |
| `AppFooter` | — | the footer row |

### `MainSection`

The main column.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `solo` | `boolean` | `false` | the column is the only one — it gets the page padding (`.solo`) |

### `ContentSection`

A block of content inside the main column, with a **measure** — how wide the
text may get.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `variant` | `'narrow-full' \| 'narrow-wide' \| 'narrow-half' \| 'null'` | `'narrow-full'` | the measure |

The measure is responsive, and it tightens as the viewport narrows:

| Variant | from 769px | from 1025px | from 1281px | from 1441px |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `narrow-full` | 640px | 640px | 680px | 680px |
| `narrow-wide` | 720px | 750px | 1024px | 1280px |
| `narrow-half` | 640px | 750px | 800px | 1024px |
| `null` | no left padding — the content goes edge to edge | | | |

### `NavSection`

A titled group of links, for a sidebar.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `title` | `string` | *required* | the group heading |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | added to the section |

```svelte
<NavSection title="Library">
	<a class="nav-link" href="/docs">Docs</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="/blog">Blog</a>
</NavSection>
```

It renders a `.nav-section` with a `.nav-header` heading and a `.box` of
children.

### `TocSection`

A table of contents, for the right rail. It takes either a list of items or
children.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `items` | `TocItem[]` | — | the entries — each becomes an anchor to `#id` |
| `title` | `string` | `'On this page'` | the heading |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | added to the section |

```svelte
<TocSection
	items={[
		{ id: 'intro', label: 'Introduction' },
		{ id: 'usage', label: 'Usage', active: true }
	]}
/>
```

Each item renders as a `.nav-link` anchor to `#id`, with `.active` on the one
you are reading. `TocItem` is `{ id: string; label: string; active?: boolean }`.

The section renders a `.toc-section` with a `.nav-header` heading and a `.box`
of the entries — the same shape as `NavSection`, so the two sit together in a
rail without looking different.

## The layout state

`layoutState` is a reactive singleton that holds the shell's regions. It exists
so that a **nested route can set its own sidebar or table of contents** without
prop drilling through every layout in between.

```svelte
<script>
	import { layoutState } from '$lib/layout';

	// in a page or a nested route
	layoutState.setRight(myTocSnippet);
	layoutState.setToc([{ id: 'intro', label: 'Introduction' }]);
</script>
```

| What | |
|:---|:---|
| `layoutState.sidebarLeft` / `.sidebarRight` / `.header` / `.footer` | the region snippets |
| `layoutState.tocItems` | the table of contents |
| `layoutState.isOpen` | whether the left drawer is open |
| `setLeft()` / `setRight()` / `setHeader()` / `setFooter()` / `setToc()` | set a region |
| `toggleSidebar(open?)` | opens, closes, or flips the drawer |
| `reset()` | clears everything |

**A prop always wins over the state.** The shell reads
`prop ?? layoutState.<region>`, so a page that passes `sidebarLeft` explicitly
keeps that, and the shared state is only the fallback.

The drawer is the other half of this: `layoutState.toggleSidebar()` sets
`isOpen`, the shell renders `.open` on it, and below 1025px the left rail
becomes a fixed drawer over the content.

## The responsive behaviour, in one place

| The viewport | What happens |
|:---|:---|
| below 1025px | the left rail is hidden — it becomes a drawer, opened with `.open` on the shell |
| from 1025px | the left rail is visible |
| from 1281px | the right rail becomes visible |
| the `--header-height` and `--footer-height` tokens | the header and footer heights; the main area is fitted to the viewport minus them, so the page never scrolls twice |

## Notes

- The components live in `src/lib/layout/`, and `index.ts` is the barrel.
  Inside this repository:

  ```js
  import { AppShell, layoutState } from '$lib/layout';
  ```

  In a project that installs the package:

  ```js
  import { AppShell, layoutState } from '@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/layout';
  ```
- The classes they render are documented in
  [Layout Shell](./07-layout-shell.md); this page is about the components
  that put them together.
- They are exported from the package under `./layout` — the components, the
  `layoutState` singleton, the `LayoutState` class and the `TocItem` type.
```

-1 : a.file > b.file ? 1 : (a.line ?? 0) - (b.line ?? 0) || (a.rule < b.rule ? -1 : a.rule > b.rule ? 1 : 0)));\n}\n\n/** Dedupe identical diagnostics (a file can be reached twice). */\nfunction uniq(d: Diag[]): Diag[] {\n\tconst seen = new Set<string>();\n\treturn d.filter((x) => {\n\t\tconst k = `${x.rule}|${x.file}|${x.line}|${x.message}`;\n\t\tif (seen.has(k)) return false;\n\t\tseen.add(k);\n\t\treturn true;\n\t});\n}\n\nexport function fractalstylerLines(): number {\n\treturn listDir(PATHS.fsDistStyles, 'file')\n\t\t.filter((n) => n.endsWith('.css') && n !== 'modular.css')\n\t\t.reduce((sum, n) => sum + cssCodeLines(readText(path.join(PATHS.fsDistStyles, n)) ?? ''), 0);\n}\n\n/** The highlighter must never drop or reorder characters. */\nasync function highlightSelftest(): Promise<Diag[]> {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst mod = (await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(ROOT, 'scripts/lib/highlight.selftest.ts')).href)) as { selftest: () => Promise<string[]> };\n\t\tconst failures = await mod.selftest();\n\t\treturn failures.map((m) => ({ rule: 'highlight/selftest', severity: 'error' as const, file: 'src/lib/internal/highlight.ts', line: null, message: m, fix: 'the concatenated token text must equal the input' }));\n\t} catch (err) {\n\t\treturn [{ rule: 'highlight/selftest', severity: 'error', file: 'src/lib/internal/highlight.ts', line: null, message: `selftest crashed: ${(err as Error).message}`, fix: 'fix highlight.ts' }];\n\t}\n}\n\nexport async function runGate(scope: Scope, pre?: { lib: Library; layers: LayerBuild }): Promise<GateResult> {\n\tconst layers = pre?.layers ?? buildLayers();\n\tconst lib = pre?.lib ?? analyzeLibrary();\n\tconst allow = loadAllowlist(layers);\n\tconst result: GateResult = { scope, groups: [], components: 0, passing: 0, failing: 0, errors: 0, warnings: 0, budget: null, scopeError: null };\n\n\tconst selected = lib.components.filter((c) => inScope(c, scope));\n\tif ((scope.kit || scope.name) && selected.length === 0) {\n\t\tconst kitExists = lib.components.some((c) => c.ref.kit === scope.kit) || listDir(PATHS.components, 'dir').includes(scope.kit ?? '');\n\t\tresult.scopeError = scope.name\n\t\t\t? `no component folder src/lib/components/${scope.kit}/${scope.name}`\n\t\t\t: kitExists\n\t\t\t\t? null\n\t\t\t\t: `no kit folder src/lib/components/${scope.kit}`;\n\t}\n\n\tconst exportOwners = new Map<string, string[]>();\n\tfor (const c of lib.components) {\n\t\tfor (const e of c.exports) {\n\t\t\tconst owners = exportOwners.get(e.name) ?? [];\n\t\t\tconst id = `${c.ref.kit}/${c.ref.slug}`;\n\t\t\tif (!owners.includes(id)) owners.push(id);\n\t\t\texportOwners.set(e.name, owners);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tconst ctx: GateContext = { allow, kits: lib.kits, slugs: new Set(lib.components.map((c) => c.ref.slug)), exportOwners };\n\n\tif (!allow.registryFound) {\n\t\tresult.groups.push({\n\t\t\tid: '(library)',\n\t\t\tkind: 'library',\n\t\t\tdiagnostics: [{ rule: 'class/registry', severity: 'error', file: 'node_modules/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/registry.json', line: null, message: 'fractalstyler registry.json not found', fix: 'pnpm install' }]\n\t\t});\n\t}\n\n\tfor (const c of selected) {\n\t\tconst diagnostics = sortDiags(uniq(checkComponent(c, ctx)));\n\t\tresult.groups.push({ id: `${c.ref.kit}/${c.ref.slug}`, kind: 'component', diagnostics });\n\t}\n\n\tconst styles = checkKitFragments(layers, lib.kits, scope.kit);\n\tif (styles.length || !scope.kit) result.groups.push({ id: '(styles)', kind: 'styles', diagnostics: sortDiags(styles) });\n\n\tif (!scope.kit) {\n\t\tconst libraryDiags = [...checkLibraryFiles(allow), ...(await highlightSelftest())];\n\t\tresult.groups.push({ id: '(library)', kind: 'library', diagnostics: sortDiags(uniq(libraryDiags)) });\n\t\tresult.budget = { maxima: layers.codeLines, fractalstyler: fractalstylerLines() };\n\t}\n\n\t// merge duplicate (library) groups\n\tconst merged: GateGroup[] = [];\n\tfor (const g of result.groups) {\n\t\tconst prev = merged.find((m) => m.id === g.id);\n\t\tif (prev) prev.diagnostics.push(...g.diagnostics);\n\t\telse merged.push(g);\n\t}\n\tresult.groups = merged;\n\n\tfor (const g of result.groups) {\n\t\tconst errs = g.diagnostics.filter((d) => d.severity === 'error').length;\n\t\tresult.errors += errs;\n\t\tresult.warnings += g.diagnostics.length - errs;\n\t\tif (g.kind === 'component') {\n\t\t\tresult.components++;\n\t\t\tif (errs) result.failing++;\n\t\t\telse result.passing++;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn result;\n}\n\nexport function formatGate(r: GateResult, opts: { quiet?: boolean } = {}): string {\n\tconst lines: string[] = [];\n\tif (r.scopeError) lines.push(`✘ ${r.scopeError}`);\n\tfor (const g of r.groups) {\n\t\tconst errs = g.diagnostics.filter((d) => d.severity === 'error').length;\n\t\tif (opts.quiet && g.diagnostics.length === 0) continue;\n\t\tif (g.kind !== 'component' && g.diagnostics.length === 0) continue;\n\t\tlines.push(`${errs ? '✘' : '✔'} ${g.id}`);\n\t\tconst ruleWidth = Math.max(0, ...g.diagnostics.map((d) => d.rule.length));\n\t\tfor (const d of g.diagnostics) {\n\t\t\tconst loc = d.line ? `${d.file}:${d.line}` : d.file;\n\t\t\tlines.push(`    ${d.severity === 'warning' ? '⚠ ' : ''}${d.rule.padEnd(ruleWidth)}  ${loc}  ${d.message}  → ${d.fix}`);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tlines.push(`${r.components} components, ${r.passing} passing, ${r.failing} failing, ${r.errors} errors${r.warnings ? `, ${r.warnings} warnings` : ''}`);\n\tif (r.budget) {\n\t\tconst pct = r.budget.fractalstyler ? ((r.budget.maxima / r.budget.fractalstyler) * 100).toFixed(1) : '—';\n\t\tlines.push(`budget: maxima extension CSS ${r.budget.maxima} lines vs fractalstyler ${r.budget.fractalstyler} lines (${pct}%)`);\n\t}\n\treturn lines.join('\\n');\n}\n"

export interface NavigationLike {
	/** Where the navigation came from. */

	/** Where the navigation is going. */
	to: { url: URL } | null;
	/** The navigation type (`link`, `goto`, `popstate`, `form`, …). */
	type: string;

	delta?: number;

	complete: Promise<void>;

export function initTheme(options: InitThemeOptions = {}): void {
	const { defaults, storageKey = STORAGE_KEY } = options;
	if (defaults) theme.set(defaults);

	$effect(() => {
		if (storageKey) {
			try {
				const stored = localStorage.getItem(storageKey);

			} catch {

		}
	});

}

export function vtName(name: string | null | undefined): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		if (name === null || name === undefined || name === '') {
			node.style.removeProperty('--vt-name');
			return;
		}
		let ident = name.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '-');
		if (/^(?:\d|-\d|--)/.test(ident) || ident === '-') ident = `vt-${ident}`;

This file is the **contract**. Every rule below is enforced by a script
(`pnpm gate`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`). If a rule and a script disagree, the
script is the truth — fix the file, never the gate.

## 0. Commands

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm dev` | the docs site (every component page is generated from the component folder) |
| `pnpm gen` | regenerate everything generated: `custom.css`, spring tokens, the barrel, `api.json` |
| `pnpm verify <kit>/<name>` | gen + gate + lint + type-check for ONE component — run this before you say "done" |
| `pnpm verify <kit>` | the same, for a whole kit |
| `pnpm gate` | the component↔docs contract for the whole library |
| `pnpm lint` | the fractalstyler closed-world linter |
| `pnpm check` | gen + svelte-check + lint + gate (the whole tree) |
| `pnpm build` | docs site + the publishable package |

Node 26, pnpm 11, Svelte 5.57 (runes only), SvelteKit 3, TypeScript 6 strict.

## 1. The two laws

### Law 1 — fractalstyler only

Styling is **composition of registered classes in markup**. Nothing else.

- NO `<style>` blocks. NO `style="…"`. NO `style:prop` directives.
- NO raw hex colours, NO pixel literals above 2px, NO literal `border-radius`.
- NO inline `<svg>` and NO unicode glyph icons — icons are
  `import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons'` +
  `import { luCheck } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide'` → `<Icon icon={luCheck} />`.
  (Check a name exists: `grep -c "luName\b" node_modules/@fractaldesign/icons/dist/lucide.d.ts`.)
- Every class must exist in **fractalstyler's registry**
  (`node_modules/@fractaldesign/fractalstyler/registry.md` — read it) or in the
  **maxima extension layer** (`src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` — read them; they
  are short).
- Modifiers are never standalone: `.row.xcenter`, never a bare `.xcenter`.
- There is no `.w-*`, `.pad-x-*`, `.border-top`. Search the registry; never guess.

**Dynamic values travel through custom properties.** JavaScript may write
*only* custom properties — `node.style.setProperty('--x', …)` — and a class
owns the real property (`translate: calc(var(--mx, 0) * 1px) …`). Use the
`vars()` attachment (`src/lib/motion`) to bind values:
`<div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: 0.4 })}>`. Never assign
`node.style.transform = …` or any real property.

**The extension layer is small on purpose.** Compose first. If the system
genuinely cannot express something, add the *smallest general primitive* to
your kit's fragment `src/lib/styles/layers/kits/<kit>.css`:

- plain CSS, tokens only (`var(--space-*)`, `var(--radius-*)`, colour roles),
  `rem`/`em`/`%` — no px above 2, no hex, no `&` nesting;
- named in the system's voice (`.track`, `.thumb`, `.indicator`) — a
  primitive several components could use, not `.my-component-inner`;
- hard budget: **90 lines per kit fragment**. The gate fails above it;
- only edit your own kit's fragment. Never edit `custom.css` (generated) or
  another layer file. After editing run `pnpm gen`.

### Law 2 — a component and its documentation are one

A component is a **folder**. It is not done until the folder passes
`pnpm verify <kit>/<name>`:

```
src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/        # <name> is kebab-case
  <Name>.svelte                         # the primary component (PascalCase of <name>)
  <NamePart>.svelte …                   # optional further parts (DialogTitle.svelte)
  <name>.svelte.ts | <name>.ts          # optional logic/state modules
  index.ts                              # named exports of every public thing
  doc.ts                                # the documentation manifest
  examples/01-usage.svelte              # ≥ 1, ordered by numeric prefix
  examples/02-….svelte
```

The docs page is **generated** from that folder — you never write a route:

- **Install / import** — generated from the package name and `index.ts`.
- **Examples** — each example file is rendered live *and* shown as source
  (the same file, so demo and code cannot drift).
- **API tables** — extracted from each part's `interface Props` and its JSDoc.
- **Accessibility / keyboard** — from `doc.ts`.

What the gate requires:

1. `index.ts` exports the primary component and every part
   (`export { default as Button } from './Button.svelte';`).
2. Every exported `.svelte` part declares `interface Props` in its instance
   script. **Every prop has a JSDoc comment** (one sentence or more). Defaults
   are documented by the destructuring default or an explicit `@default` tag.
3. `doc.ts` default-exports `defineDoc({...})` (shape below), nothing empty.
4. Each example starts with the header line
   `<!-- @example Title :: One sentence describing what it shows. -->`
   and example 01 is the minimal usage.
5. **Coverage — nothing is left out.** Across the folder's examples:
   every value of every string-literal-union prop (`variant`, `size`, `shape`,
   `placement`, …) appears; every prop name declared in `Props` (of every part)
   appears. (`class`, `children`, `ref` are exempt.)
6. Law 1, statically: no style blocks/attributes/directives, no `<svg`, no
   `.style.` writes other than `setProperty('--…')`, and every class token in a
   `class="…"` / `class={…}` literal is registered.
7. Inside `src/lib`, imports are **relative** (no `#lib`, no `$lib`). Examples
   import only from `@fractaldesign/maxima-ui` (and `/motion`, `/theme`),
   `@fractaldesign/icons*`, and `svelte*` — exactly what a consumer would write.

### `doc.ts`

```ts
import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',                       // the primary export
	summary: 'One sentence. Shown in the index and the page header.',
	description: `One to three paragraphs. Blank line = new paragraph. \`code\` allowed.`,
	parts: { ButtonGroup: 'One line: what this part is for.' },   // optional, every non-primary .svelte export
	features: ['Spring-pressed', '…'],    // optional bullets
	accessibility: ['Renders a native <button> …'],               // ≥ 1
	keyboard: [{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' }],   // when interactive
	api: [{ name: 'toast(message, options?)', type: '(…) => string', description: '…' }], // non-component exports
	related: ['icon-button']              // optional slugs
});

## 2. Authoring conventions

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { sizeClass, type Size, type Shape, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style of the button. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The content. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let { variant = 'primary', size = 'md', class: klass, children, ...rest }: Props = $props();
</script>

<button class={['button', variant, sizeClass[size], klass]} {...rest}>
	{@render children?.()}
</button>
```

- Runes only: `$props`, `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$bindable`,
  `$props.id()` for ids. Snippets, never slots. `{@attach}`, never `use:`.
  Callback props (`onchange`), never `createEventDispatcher`.
- `class` is always accepted and merged last via the array form
  `class={['…', cond && '…', klass]}`. Spread `...rest` onto the root element
  and extend the matching `svelte/elements` attribute type.
- Two-way state is `$bindable()` **and** has a callback
  (`value = $bindable()`, `onValueChange`). Works controlled and uncontrolled.
- Shared axes come from `src/lib/internal/tokens.ts` — do not redefine:
  `Variant` (`primary secondary themed outline ghost link soft info success
  warning danger`), `Size` (`xs sm md lg xl` → `sizeClass[size]`), `Shape`
  (`rect mincurved modern curved round`), `Tone` (`neutral info success
  warning danger`), `Placement`.
- Compound components share state with `createContext` from `svelte`
  (`const [getTabs, setTabs] = createContext<TabsState>()`).
- Use the platform first: native `<dialog>`, the Popover API (`popover`
  attribute), CSS anchor positioning (`.anchor` / `.floating`, see
  `src/lib/internal/floating.ts`), `<details>`, `:has()`, `@starting-style`
  enter/exit (`.pop` + `.enter-*`). JavaScript only where the platform stops.
- SSR-safe: no `window`/`document` at module or init time — only inside
  `$effect`, attachments and event handlers.
- Accessible by construction: correct roles, `aria-*` wiring, labels, focus
  management, full keyboard support (document it in `doc.ts`).
- Motion (all from `src/lib/motion`): springs for anything a user moves or
  triggers; honour reduced motion (the motion layer already does — do not
  bypass it). Prefer CSS spring tokens (`.spring.snappy`, `.pop`) for
  state-driven motion; the JS spring engine (`animate`, `SpringValue`, the
  attachments) for gestures and layout.
- No new dependencies. No `any`. No `@ts-ignore`. No TODOs.
- Aesthetic bar: restrained, precise, premium. Hairline borders, the
  elevation ladder, generous but consistent spacing from the space ladder,
  `text-secondary`/`text-muted` for hierarchy, `.rim` + `.shad-*` on raised
  surfaces, `.glass` on floating ones, tabular numerals for numbers. Examples
  use realistic content (real product copy, never "foo"/"Lorem ipsum").

## 3. Map

| | |
|:---|:---|
| `src/lib/styles/layers/*.css` | the maxima extension layer — sources. `kits/<kit>.css` are the kit fragments |
| `src/lib/styles/custom.css` | GENERATED concat of the layers — fractalstyler's sanctioned `custom.css` extension point; the linter reads it |
| `src/lib/internal/` | shared tokens, floating/anchor helpers, list navigation, highlight |
| `src/lib/motion/` | spring solver, CSS spring tokens, `animate`, attachments, transitions, view transitions |
| `src/lib/theme/` | parametric theme runtime (mode, theme, hue/chroma, radius, density, motion) |
| `src/lib/components/<kit>/<name>/` | the components — see Law 2 |
| `src/lib/components/kits.ts` | the kit list (order, titles) |
| `src/lib/docs/` | `defineDoc`, doc types, GENERATED `api.json` |
| `src/lib/index.ts` | GENERATED barrel |
| `src/routes/` | the docs site — generated pages + hand-written guides |
| `scripts/` | `gen.ts`, `gate.ts`, `verify.ts` and friends |

Generated files carry a `GENERATED` banner — never edit them by hand.

## 4. House rules

- fractalstyler is consumed from `../fractalstyler` (linked). **Never edit
  anything in `../fractalstyler`.** Missing primitives go in the extension layer.
- Do not initialise git, commit, push or publish unless the user asks.
- Work only in the paths you were assigned; other agents are working in
  parallel in sibling folders. Never "fix" a sibling's files — report instead.

## 5. Motion and theme quick reference

Import inside `src/lib` from `'../../../motion/index.js'` / `'../../../theme/index.js'`;
in examples from `'@fractaldesign/maxima-ui/motion'` / `'/theme'` (also re-exported
from the root). Read the sources for the full JSDoc.

```ts
// springs — presets: 'gentle' | 'snappy' | 'bouncy' | 'stiff' | 'slow', or { stiffness, damping, mass }
springs, resolveSpring(input?), springDuration(input?), springEasing(input?), springEase(input?)

// engine — element must carry class "motion" (x y scale rotate opacity) or "tilt" (rotateX rotateY)
animate(node, { x, y, scale, rotate, opacity, rotateX, rotateY, '--custom': n }, { spring, instant, onUpdate }) → { finished, stop() }
setMotion(node, values)   getMotion(node, channel)
new SpringValue(initial, spring?)  → .current (reactive) .target .set(v, { instant })
reducedMotion.current

// attachments — {@attach name(options)}
vars({ value: 0.4 })                    // writes --value (any custom properties)
press() hover() magnetic() tilt()       // interaction springs
pointer()                               // writes --px/--py for spotlights
inView({ class: 'in' }) reveal() stagger()   // entrance; stagger writes --i on children
drag({ axis, bounds, snapBack, momentum, onDragEnd })
parallax() scrollProgress()
createFlip() → { attach, read(), play(), run(fn) }   // FLIP layout springs; items carry data-flip-id

// Svelte transitions with spring easing — transition:springScale={{ spring: 'bouncy' }}
springFade springFly springScale springBlur springSlide

// view transitions
startViewTransition(update, { type: 'fade'|'slide'|'slide-back'|'scale'|'reveal'|'none', origin })
setupViewTransitions(onNavigate, { type })    vtName('hero')   // element also needs class "vt-name"

// theme
theme (ThemeState: mode theme hue chroma tint radius density motion resolvedMode; setTheme() setMode() toggleMode(event) reset())
themes, initTheme(), themeInitScript()
```

CSS side (see `src/lib/styles/layers/10-motion.css`): `.spring` + `.spring-<preset>`
for state transitions, `.pop` + `.enter-*` for anything that opens (works on
`[popover]`, `<dialog open>`, and `.open`), `.anim-in` (staggered by `--i`),
`.reveal`/`.in`, `.lift`, `.press`.

# DESIGN

The design language of maxima-ui. It is fractalstyler's language, held to a
premium bar — restrained, precise, quiet until touched.

## Principles

1. **Composition over invention.** A component is a sentence written in
   fractalstyler's vocabulary. If two components look related, it is because
   they share classes, not because someone matched them by eye.
2. **Hierarchy through ink, not size.** `text-primary` → `text-secondary` →
   `text-muted` carry most hierarchy. Size and weight change rarely.
3. **Hairlines and light.** Surfaces are separated by 1px borders
   (`border`, `border-subtle`) and lifted by the elevation ladder (`shad-*`)
   with a lit top edge (`rim`). Floating surfaces are `glass`.
4. **Motion is physics.** Anything a person moves or triggers is driven by a
   spring — the same solver produces the CSS `linear()` tokens
   (`--spring-snappy` …) and drives the JavaScript engine, so a CSS transition
   and a dragged element settle the same way. Motion is interruptible, never
   blocks input, and collapses to nothing under reduced motion.
5. **One theme, three numbers.** `--hue`, `--chroma`, `--tint` generate every
   colour role in both modes. Shape (`data-radius`), density (`data-density`)
   and motion (`data-motion`) are independent axes that rewrite ladders, not
   components.

## The shared axes

| Axis | Values | Mechanism |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `variant` | primary · secondary · themed · soft · outline · ghost · link · info · success · warning · danger | a class of the same name |
| `size` | xs · sm · md · lg · xl | `sizeClass[size]` → height + text ladder |
| `shape` | rect · mincurved · modern · curved · round | a class of the same name |
| `tone` | neutral · info · success · warning · danger | status colour roles |

## The extension layer

| Layer | Adds |
|:---|:---|

<script lang="ts">
	import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
	import type { HTMLAnchorAttributes, HTMLButtonAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';
	import { Icon } from '@fractaldesign/icons';
	import type { IconData } from '@fractaldesign/icons';
	import { luLoaderCircle } from '@fractaldesign/icons/lucide';
	import { press } from '../../../motion/index.js';
	import { sizeClass, type Shape, type Size, type Variant } from '../../../internal/tokens.js';

	interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes {
		/** The visual style. `primary` is the page's main action; use one per view. */
		variant?: Variant;
		/** The control height and text scale. */
		size?: Size;
		/** The corner shape. */
		shape?: Shape;
		/** An icon drawn before the label. */
		icon?: IconData;
		/** An icon drawn after the label. */
		iconEnd?: IconData;
		/** Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and blocks interaction, keeping the button's width. */
		loading?: boolean;
		/** Stretches the button to the full width of its container. */
		block?: boolean;
		/** Renders an `<a>` that looks like a button. Use for navigation. */
		href?: string;
		/** Where to open the link, when `href` is set. */
		target?: HTMLAnchorAttributes['target'];
		/** Springs the button down under the pointer. Turn off for a still button. */
		pressable?: boolean;
		/** The label. */
		children?: Snippet;
	}

	let {
		variant = 'primary',
		size = 'md',
		shape = 'modern',
		icon,
		iconEnd,
		loading = false,
		block = false,
		href,
		target,
		pressable = true,
		disabled,
		type = 'button',
		class: klass,
		children,
		...rest
	}: Props = $props();

	const classes = $derived([
		'button no-scaling gap-sm weight-500',
		variant,
		sizeClass[size],
		shape,
		block ? 'wfull' : 'inline-flex',
		pressable && 'motion',
		klass
	]);
	const spring = $derived(pressable ? press() : undefined);
</script>

{#snippet content()}
	{#if loading}
		<Icon icon={luLoaderCircle} class="anim-spin" />
	{:else if icon}
		<Icon {icon} />
	{/if}
	{@render children?.()}
	{#if iconEnd}
		<Icon icon={iconEnd} />
	{/if}
{/snippet}

{#if href && !disabled}
	<a
		class={classes}
		{href}
		{target}
		rel={target === '_blank' ? 'noopener noreferrer' : undefined}
		aria-busy={loading || undefined}
		{@attach spring}
		{...rest as HTMLAnchorAttributes}
	>
		{@render content()}
	</a>
{:else}
	<button
		class={classes}
		{type}
		disabled={disabled || loading}
		aria-busy={loading || undefined}
		{@attach spring}
		{...rest}
	>
		{@render content()}
	</button>
{/if}

import { defineDoc } from '../../../docs/define.js';

export default defineDoc({
	name: 'Button',
	summary: 'Triggers an action or navigates, with a spring-loaded press.',
	description: `The button is the library's reference component: eleven variants, five sizes and five shapes, all of them plain fractalstyler classes, so a button always matches the inputs, tags and cards around it.

It renders a native \`<button>\` — or an \`<a>\` when you pass \`href\` — and forwards every attribute and event to it. Pressing it drives a real spring through the motion channel rather than a CSS keyframe, so a quick tap and a long hold both feel right.`,
	features: [
		'Eleven variants, five sizes, five shapes — shared with every other control',
		'Leading and trailing icons from @fractaldesign/icons',
		'Loading state that keeps the layout stable',
		'Renders a link when given href',
		'Interruptible spring press, disabled under reduced motion'
	],
	accessibility: [
		'Renders a native <button> (or <a> with href), so role, focus and activation come from the platform.',
		'While loading, the button is disabled and exposes aria-busy="true".',
		'An icon-only button needs an aria-label; icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.',
		'The focus ring is drawn only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible).'
	],
	keyboard: [
		{ keys: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the button.' },
		{ keys: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the next focusable element.' }
	]
});

import type { Attachment } from 'svelte/attachments';

/** The CSS anchor name for an id — `$props.id()` output is a fine id. */
export function anchorName(id: string): string {
	return `--anchor-${id.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '')}`;
}

/**
 * Pair a trigger with its floating element. Put `{@attach anchor(id)}` on the
 * trigger (with class `anchor`) and `{@attach floating(id)}` on the floating
 * element (with class `floating at-…`): both receive the same `--anchor`
 * name, and CSS anchor positioning does the rest.
 */
export function anchor(id: string): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		node.style.setProperty('--anchor', anchorName(id));
		return () => node.style.removeProperty('--anchor');
	};
}

/** The floating side of `anchor()`. `offset` overrides the gap (any CSS length or token). */
export function floating(id: string, offset?: string): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		node.style.setProperty('--anchor', anchorName(id));
		if (offset) node.style.setProperty('--offset', offset);
		return () => {
			node.style.removeProperty('--anchor');
			node.style.removeProperty('--offset');
		};
	};
}

/**
 * Keep a boolean in step with a native popover element.
 * Returns an attachment for the `[popover]` element: it shows/hides the
 * popover when `isOpen()` changes and reports user dismissal through `onChange`.
 */
export function popoverSync(
	isOpen: () => boolean,
	onChange: (open: boolean) => void
): Attachment<HTMLElement> {
	return (node) => {
		const want = isOpen();
		const shown = node.matches(':popover-open');
		if (want && !shown) node.showPopover();
		else if (!want && shown) node.hidePopover();

		const onToggle = (event: Event) => {
			const next = (event as ToggleEvent).newState === 'open';
			if (next !== isOpen()) onChange(next);
		};
		node.addEventListener('toggle', onToggle);
		return () => node.removeEventListener('toggle', onToggle);
	};
}

/**
 * The same for a native `<dialog>`: opens modally when `isOpen()` turns true,
 * closes when it turns false, and reports Esc / backdrop dismissal.
 */
export function dialogSync(
	isOpen: () => boolean,
	onChange: (open: boolean) => void,
	options: { modal?: boolean; dismissible?: boolean } = {}
): Attachment<HTMLDialogElement> {
	return (node) => {
		const { modal = true, dismissible = true } = options;
		const want = isOpen();
		if (want && !node.open) {
			if (modal) node.showModal();
			else node.show();
		} else if (!want && node.open) node.close();

		const onClose = () => {
			if (isOpen()) onChange(false);
		};
		const onCancel = (event: Event) => {
			if (!dismissible) event.preventDefault();
		};
		// A click that lands on the dialog element itself is a click on the backdrop.
		const onClick = (event: MouseEvent) => {
			if (dismissible && event.target === node) node.close();
		};
		node.addEventListener('close', onClose);
		node.addEventListener('cancel', onCancel);
		node.addEventListener('click', onClick);
		return () => {
			node.removeEventListener('close', onClose);
			node.removeEventListener('cancel', onCancel);
			node.removeEventListener('click', onClick);
		};
	};
}
